title: StrokePath
description: Realot Studio StrokePath component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.
headings: How to add and use StrokePath
What you should see after adding it
content: Scope This page documents the StrokePath component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts. Where to find it in the editor Top GameObject → 2D Object → Stroke Path. After a Stroke Path exists, the toolbar exposes Path (P); click empty space to append, drag points, and click segments to insert. What it does A variable-thickness strip along placed points — rivers, cables, roads, conveyor belts or walls — with flat color or textured fill. Component setup & editor tools StrokePath creates a drawable strip/path; its editing is performed with the Stroke Path viewport tool/gizmo. How to add and use StrokePath Editor path: Select the target entity in the Hierarchy (left side) → look at the Inspector (right side) → click Add Component at the bottom of the Inspector → search for StrokePath → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached. For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool. Component setup & editor tools Select an entity with StrokePath → use the Stroke Path viewport tool/gizmo to edit path points. Keep the Inspector open for serialized path/material settings. What you should see after adding it The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the Component data table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable. How to read the settings For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes type , default , meaning , and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in Coordinate system ; do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions. Component data Field Type Purpose Default points array Two default points (a minimal, visibly-a-path starting shape) rather than one or zero — a single point has no strip to draw at all, so a StrokePath freshly added via the GameObject menu or Add Component window shows *something* immediately instead of an invisible/degenerate result the user has to fix before they can… [{x:-100,y:0}, {x:100,y:0}] thickness number Strip thickness. 40 color hex color string Flat fill color, used when useTexture is false. #8a8a8a opacity number Opacity. 1 useTexture boolean Use an image texture along the path instead of a flat fill. false textureKey nullable value Logical sprite key, resolved to a PIXI.Texture the same way SpriteRenderer.spriteKey is (see runtime/assets/AssetManager.js resolveTexture) — components never hold PIXI objects directly, for the same "stay serializable" reason SpriteRenderer doesn't. null textureMode StrokePathTextureMode enum: stretch | tile See StrokePathTextureMode above — STRETCH (fit the whole image to the path, may distort) or TILE (repeat at native size, never stretched). stretch textureTiling number TILE mode only: how many world units of path length one full texture tile covers lengthwise — e.g. 100 textureScale number How many times the texture repeats ACROSS the strip's own thickness (perpendicular to the direction of travel) — kept separate from textureTiling (the lengthwise axis) since a texture like a road stripe or brick run almost always needs a different repeat rate across its width than along its length. 1 textureOffset number Slides the texture lengthwise along the path without moving any point — e.g. 0 textureFlip boolean Mirrors the texture across the path's own centerline (flips which side is "up") without needing a second, mirrored copy of the source image — handy for a texture that's only authored for one direction of travel. false textureRotation number Rotates the texture, in degrees, around the center of each tile — independent of every other texture setting above, and applied in TEXTURE space (not world space), so it stays a fixed "printed at an angle on the image" look rather than a rotation that would need to track the path's own direction as it turns. 0 jointMode StrokePathJointMode enum: sharp | bevel | round See StrokePathJointMode above — SHARP (hard corner), BEVEL (flat chamfer), or ROUND (filled arc). round capMode StrokePathCapMode enum: none | box | round See StrokePathCapMode above — NONE (flat stop), BOX (flat, but extended slightly past the tip), or ROUND (half-circle cap). round smoothing number 0-1. Runs the authored `points` through a Catmull-Rom spline resample BEFORE tessellation, turning the raw straight-segment polyline into a smooth curve — same idea as a spline/curve tool in a 3D package, applied to this 2D strip. 0 Tuning behavior These are the practical direction-of-change rules for the most important controls on this component. Setting What changing it does thickness Larger values make the strip wider. textureTiling In TILE mode, larger values make each repeated texture cover more path length, so the image repeats less often. textureScale Higher scales the texture; lower makes it smaller/repeated more densely. textureOffset Changing this over time scrolls the texture along the path. opacity 0 invisible, 1 opaque. The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. textureTiling Property (read/write) The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on (read/write) The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. worldToLocal(worldX, worldY) Method The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. Notes & behavior Points are placed with the Path tool in the Scene viewport, then adjusted by dragging a point or clicking a segment to insert a new one between two existing points. An open polyline (A to B), not a closed loop. Reads/writes on this.strokePath.points always operate on a copy, so mutating a returned array can never silently corrupt the live component; assign it back (or use the point methods) to apply a change. Examples js this . strokePath . addPoint ( this . x , this . y ); js this . strokePath . textureOffset += 20 * time . deltaTime ; // flowing river/conveyor look Need the full workflow? For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool. Component setup & editor tools Select an entity in the Hierarchy; edit Transform fields in the Inspector. Use the Scene viewport transform gizmo to move/rotate/scale visually. What you should see after adding it The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the Component data table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable. How to read the settings For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes type , default , meaning , and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in Coordinate system ; do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions. Component data Field Type Purpose Default x number World position X. 0 y number World position Y. 0 z number Pseudo-3D depth; affects sprite scale only when Camera.enablePseudo3D is enabled. 0 rotation number Rotation in degrees around Z. 0 scaleX number Horizontal scale multiplier. 1 scaleY number Vertical scale multiplier. 1 Tuning behavior These are the practical direction-of-change rules for the most important controls on this component. Setting What changing it does x / y World position. Increasing X moves right; increasing Y moves down in the engine’s 2D world convention. rotation Degrees clockwise visually in the screen coordinate convention; 0 points along +X for directional/spot light orientation. scaleX / scaleY 1 is native scale; >1 enlarges; 0.5 halves size; negative values mirror the corresponding axis. Script API Member Kind Description lookAt(x, y) Method Point the entity toward a world-space point. position Property (read/write) { x, y } world-space position; read or assign. rotation Property (read/write) Rotation in degrees. scale Property (read/write) Exposed by this script module. translate(dx, dy) Method Move by a delta amount. Examples js this . position = { x : 200 , y : 120 }; js this . rotation = 45 ; js this . translate ( 50 * time . deltaTime , 0 ); Need the full workflow? title: API reference
description: Complete Realot Studio component, script-module and runtime API reference.
content: Start with prerequisites The API requirements & complete usage map shows which components or scene systems must exist before an API can be used. Components The editor's component system contains 25 documented component types. Each component page lists its public scene fields, defaults, field descriptions, and the script API members exposed when that component is attached. Transform Position, rotation and scale. SpriteRenderer Texture, color, flips and opacity. ShapeRenderer Procedural square, circle, capsule and triangle shapes. TextRenderer World-space and screen-space text. StrokePath Editable variable-width lines and textured paths. SpeechBubble Entity-attached dialogue bubble. ChatLog Scrollable message history. TextInput Interactive text entry. Joystick Virtual touch joystick. Rigidbody2D Static, Dynamic and Kinematic physics body. Collider2D Collision shape, triggers and layer filters. Joint2D Fixed, Revolute, Prismatic, Rope and Spring joints. CharacterController Character, Platformer, Top-Down, Car, Follow, Patrol and Free movement modes. SpriteAnimation Sprite-sheet clips and animation state. Camera Reference resolution, scaling, follow, shake and pseudo-3D. AudioSource Playback, pitch, volume and spatial attenuation. AudioListener Hearing radius and audio detection. Light Six 2D light modes. ShadowCaster Shadow occlusion geometry and softness. LightingSettings Scene-wide ambient and shadow quality settings. NavAgent2D Pathfinding, area filters, avoidance and vehicle tuning. NavWorld2D Shared painted or baked navigation grid. Tileset Reusable 16-role autotile setup. Tilemap Painted tile grid linked to a Tileset. Script Script name, source and enabled state. Complete script-module index The Script module member index is generated from the engine's supported-member sets. It covers every member exposed by the this.* component modules, plus this.state , this.myTouch , scene.lighting and the global save API. Each entry includes its access type, context and source file. Global runtime API Scripts also receive global functions and objects such as findFirst() , scene , physics , nav , input , mouse , touch , time , random , mathx , save , debug and pool . See Runtime modules and the practical Global API guide . Option shapes and requirements Optional arguments for raycasts, spawning, navigation, camera follow and other script calls are documented in Option schemas (opts) . The requirements map identifies component prerequisites and always-available APIs. Machine-readable catalog For code tools and AI assistants, fetch api/index.json . It contains component field/default metadata, lifecycle callbacks, enum values, global API groups, all 24 script API modules and their supported member lists. The full manual is available from llms-full.txt ; the search index is search-index.json .

title: Option schemas & opts
description: Exact option objects, types, defaults and semantics for the most important Realot Studio APIs, with machine-readable JSON for tooling and LLMs.
content: Need to know what must exist first? Use the API requirements & complete usage map to see prerequisites for every global and component API. Hands-on examples See the Script API cookbook for complete scripts showing where each API lives and how the pieces fit together. Authoritative option metadata Navigation option names are defined once in runtime/scripting/NavAPI.js and consumed by both runtime behavior and editor IntelliSense. The machine-readable api-options.json mirrors the documented public option groups. nav.findPath Option Type Default Effect debug boolean False Draw the current path as green debug segments for one frame. radius number 0 Agent clearance against the shared NavWorld2D. Larger radius can close narrow passages. area number 65535 16-bit allowed-area mask. Default 0xffff allows every area. areaCosts number[]|null None Per-call 16-slot cost overrides; null entries use NavWorld2D defaults. this.navMoveToward Option Type Default Effect repathInterval number 0.35 Seconds between re-path checks when autoRepath is enabled. arriveDist number 4 Distance at which an intermediate waypoint is considered reached. finalArriveDist number 1 Distance from final target considered arrived. targetChangeDistance number 4 Target movement that forces an immediate re-path; effective default is max(4, arriveDist). debug boolean False Draw the current path as green debug segments for one frame. this.navDriveToward Option Type Default Effect repathInterval number 0.35 Seconds between re-path checks when autoRepath is enabled. arriveDist number 4 Distance at which an intermediate waypoint is considered reached. finalArriveDist number 1 Distance from final target considered arrived. targetChangeDistance number 4 Target movement that forces an immediate re-path; effective default is max(4, arriveDist). debug boolean False Draw the current path as green debug segments for one frame. findInRadius Option Type Default Effect name string|undefined None Only return entities with this exact name. tag string|undefined None Only return entities with this exact tag when name is not provided. spawn Option Type Default Effect x number|undefined source x Spawn position X override. y number|undefined source y Spawn position Y override. name string|undefined source name Rename the clone. byTag boolean False Interpret the first argument as a tag instead of a name. physics.raycast Option Type Default Effect layerMask number|undefined engine default Restrict ray hits to collider layers included in the mask. debug boolean False Draw the ray debug line for one frame. exclude array|undefined None Exclude listed entity/entity-context targets from hit testing. mouse.isOver / clickedOn Option Type Default Effect byTag boolean False Interpret the string target as a tag instead of an entity name. touch.isOver / tappedOn Option Type Default Effect byTag boolean False Interpret the string target as a tag instead of an entity name. justStarted boolean False Only match touches that began this frame. Examples js this . navMoveToward ( target . x , target . y , 160 , { repathInterval : 0.2 , arriveDist : 6 , finalArriveDist : 12 , debug : true , }); const hits = physics . raycast ( this . x , this . y , target . x , target . y , { layerMask : 1 << 0 , exclude : [ this ], debug : true , }); How opts overrides work Realot Studio uses options in a few different ways. An explicit option normally wins for that call; otherwise the method uses the component/default value. This matters most for navigation and raycasts. Pattern What it means this.navMoveToward(x,y,160) Explicit speed is used for this call; other behavior can come from the NavAgent2D component. this.navMoveToward(x,y,160,{ finalArriveDist: 12 }) Only finalArriveDist changes for this call; unrelated options keep their defaults/component behavior. nav.findPath(...,{ radius: 24 }) Manual query uses the supplied radius instead of assuming the caller's component radius. physics.raycast(...,{ exclude:[this] }) The current entity is removed from the query results, preventing self-hits. Do not invent option names. Realot Studio is not drop-in Unity/Unreal/Godot API compatibility. Use the exact option names documented here and in the editor's IntelliSense. Navigation option recipes Hard route restriction js var route = nav . findPath ( this . x , this . y , goalX , goalY , { area : nav . areaMask ( "Road" , "Ground" ) }); Only named areas in the mask are legal. An omitted area is not a fallback route; it is forbidden. Soft route preference js var route = nav . findPath ( this . x , this . y , goalX , goalY , { area : nav . areaMask ( "Road" , "Ground" , "Mud" ), areaCosts : nav . areaCosts ({ Road : 1 , Ground : 2 , Mud : 5 }) }); All three areas remain legal, but the pathfinder prefers cheaper traversals when route length is otherwise comparable. Per-agent runtime override js var costs = this . navAgent . areaCosts || []; costs [ 2 ] = 4 ; this . navAgent . areaCosts = costs ; areaCosts is an indexed 16-slot array on the component. Assign a new normalized array back to the property; mutating a previously-read temporary is not enough unless you reassign it. LLM usage rule When generating Realot Studio code, prefer the documented option name and shape exactly as listed. Do not invent Unity/Unreal/Godot option names just because they sound familiar; Realot Studio’s runtime and IntelliSense contract is the authority.

title: API requirements & complete usage map
description: Complete prerequisites and usage map for Realot Studio scripting APIs.
content: Prerequisites matter. Realot Studio does not expose every component API on every entity. this.sprite , this.rigidbody , this.navAgent , and the other component sub-objects are created only when the corresponding component exists on that same entity. If the component is absent, the sub-object is undefined . Use this.hasComponent("...") when you need to guard optional behavior. Universal component-API workflow Select the entity in the Hierarchy . In the Inspector on the right, click Add Component . Search for the required component and click it. Configure its Inspector properties and any component-specific editor tool that appears. Add a Script component to the same entity and open/edit its script. Inside the script, access the matching sub-object, for example this.rigidbody or this.sprite . Play the scene and inspect the Console if the component is missing or an API call is invalid. js // Example: Rigidbody2D is required for this API. function onStart () { if ( ! this . rigidbody ) return ; this . rigidbody . velocity = { x : 100 , y : 0 }; } Global APIs — no component required These are injected into every running game script. They are not added through Add Component . enabled showFps stats debugLines entity point normal distance findWithTag findFirst findAll findFirstWithTag findAllWithTag findById findInRadius scene physics nav sendMessage broadcastMessage spawn wait cancelWait repeat cancelRepeat input mouse touch time random smoothstep mathx global save debug Global family Required setup Typical use scene A running scene. Load/restart/pause/resume scenes and access scene-level services. physics Physics runtime for physics queries. Raycasts and collision-layer/mask operations. nav Configured Nav World 2D for meaningful pathfinding. Find paths, test walkability, use named navigation areas/costs. input , mouse , touch Running game input; touch requires a touch-capable device for actual touch events. Keyboard, mouse, touch, swipe and pinch controls. time , random , mathx None. Frame timing, randomness and gameplay math. save Browser storage available to the deployment. Persistent save slots. debug Running game/editor debug surface. Debug messages and visual diagnostics. spawn , wait , repeat Running entity script/runtime. Runtime clones and entity-owned timers. sendMessage , broadcastMessage Running scene with target entities when targeting by name/tag. Script-to-script communication. Core transform shortcuts such as this.x , this.y , this.position , this.rotation , this.scaleX and this.scaleY are available without adding a separate Transform component. Other capabilities are deliberately grouped under their component sub-object: this.rigidbody , this.collider , this.joint , this.controller , this.sprite , this.animator , this.camera , this.audio , this.ear , this.navAgent , this.light , this.shadowCaster , this.strokePath , and the UI APIs documented above. Guarding optional components js function onUpdate ( dt ) {{ if ( this . hasComponent ( "Rigidbody2D" )) {{ // Safe to use this.rigidbody here. this . rigidbody . velocityX = 100 ; }} }} Use the exact component name expected by the engine. For systems with additional world-level prerequisites—especially navigation—having the entity component is necessary but not sufficient. How to read opts Whenever a function accepts an opts object, the reference must be read as a contract: each property has a type, default, allowed/meaningful range, and effect. Omitted properties use the documented default. Realot Studio does not expose every component API on every entity. this.sprite , this.rigidbody , this.navAgent , and the other component sub-objects are created only when the corresponding component exists on that same entity. Add a Script component to the same entity and open/edit its script. Inside the script, access the matching sub-object, for example this.rigidbody or this.sprite . title: Runtime modules and global API
description: Index of global functions and objects supplied to gameplay scripts in Realot Studio.
content: Entity lookup functions findFirst(name) , findAll(name) , findFirstWithTag(tag) , findAllWithTag(tag) , findWithTag(tag) , findById(id) and findInRadius(x, y, radius, opts?) locate entities in the current scene. Scene, physics and navigation Object Exposed surface scene Entity lookup; load , restart , pause , resume ; read-only current and isPaused ; scene-wide lighting . physics raycast(x1, y1, x2, y2, opts?) , layer(...indices) . nav findPath , isWalkable , bake , areaIndex , areaMask , areaCosts . Input, time and math Object Exposed surface input keyDown(key) , keyPressed(key) . mouse World/screen coordinates, cursor state, button state, isOver , clickedOn . touch Active touch list, per-touch positions and state, swipe/pinch helpers, isOver , tappedOn . time deltaTime , unscaledDeltaTime , elapsed , scale . random int(min, max) , float(min, max) . mathx lerp , smoothstep , clamp , moveToward , remap , approximately . smoothstep(a, b, value) Global smoothstep helper also available without mathx. . Game services Object / function Purpose global Shared in-memory key/value state between scripts during the running game. save Persistent key/value data and named save slots backed by IndexedDB; exact members are in SaveAPI . debug Play-window diagnostic HUD, FPS line and custom values. pool Named object pools for reusing entities. spawn(nameOrTag, opts?) Creates a runtime clone. wait , repeat , cancelWait , cancelRepeat Entity-owned one-shot and repeating timers. sendMessage , broadcastMessage Targeted, tag-group or scene-wide script messaging. tween , cancelTween Property animation over game time. Detailed global API guide The Global scripting API explains each object with examples. Use Input , Persistence , Pathfinding and Tween API for focused guides. Per-entity component modules Component modules such as this.rigidbody , this.sprite , this.camera and this.text depend on the components attached to the entity. The complete script module index lists every supported member from all 24 script API modules, its access type and required context. The this reference explains EntityContext shortcuts and prerequisites. Fixed update onFixedUpdate(dt) runs on the fixed physics cadence (60 steps per second in the supplied runtime). Use it for logic that should follow fixed-step physics timing; use onUpdate(dt) for frame-based presentation and input handling. Coordinate spaces Entity positions, mouse.x/y , touch x/y , raycast points and navigation waypoints use world-space coordinates. Mouse/touch screenX/screenY values are raw game-canvas pixels. Camera reference resolution and world units are separate concepts.

title: this (EntityContext) reference
description: Complete reference for the current entity context, all flat shortcuts, pointer/touch helpers, navigation methods and per-entity script modules.
content: Transform shortcuts Every entity has a Transform. These members read or write its live data; position values use world-space coordinates and rotation is in degrees. Member Access Meaning x , y Read/write World position coordinates. Writes also update the physics body's position target when a Rigidbody2D is attached. position Read/write Gets or assigns an {x, y} object. rotation Read/write Rotation in degrees. Kinematic bodies receive the script-set rotation target. scaleX , scaleY Read/write Transform scale factors. translate(dx, dy) Method Moves the entity by a relative world-space offset and synchronizes physics position targeting. distanceTo(x, y) Method Returns straight-line distance from the entity to a world-space point. transform Sub-object Always available; see TransformAPI . Identity, visibility and lifecycle members Member Access Meaning name Read-only Entity name. tag Read/write Entity tag; can be changed while the game runs. id Read-only Stable unique entity ID. Prefer this when you need to refer to one exact spawned instance. visible Read/write Gets or sets the entity's active/visible state. enabled Read/write Gets or sets the enabled state of the Script component attached to this entity. Without a Script component, reads as enabled. destroy() Method Queues this entity for removal at the end of the current frame; it is not torn down in the middle of the callback. destroyed Read-only True after destroy() is queued and before the entity is removed. hasComponent(componentKey) Method Tests whether the entity currently has a component, for example hasComponent("Rigidbody2D") . Every entity has Transform. isClone Read-only True for the context used by a script on an entity created by runtime spawn() . spawn(nameOrTagOrEntity, opts) Method Creates a runtime clone. Accepts a name/tag lookup or an EntityContext. See Finding and spawning . wait(seconds, callback) , cancelWait(timerId) Methods Start and cancel an entity-owned one-shot timer. repeat(seconds, callback) , cancelRepeat(timerId) Methods Start and cancel an entity-owned repeating timer. releaseToPool(delay?) Method Returns a pooled entity to its pool immediately or after an optional delay. isPooled Read-only True when the entity was created and is managed by an object pool. Pointer and touch helpers These helpers test the current entity's actual Collider2D shape, not only its bounding rectangle. A Collider2D is required ; without one these hit tests cannot match the pointer or a finger. Member Meaning Input isPointerOver True while the mouse cursor is over this entity. Mouse hover. isClicked True for the frame the left mouse button is pressed over this entity. Mouse click. isTouchOver True while any active finger is over this entity. Touch hover. isTapped True for the frame a finger first touches down over this entity. Touch tap. myTouch Per-entity tracking for claiming and following one finger. The sub-object exists on every entity, but hit detection requires Collider2D. See TouchTrackAPI . Navigation movement methods Method Requirements Behavior navMoveToward(targetX, targetY, speed?, opts?) NavWorld2D for pathfinding. NavAgent2D is optional but supplies radius, speed, repath, area and avoidance defaults. Finds a path and advances the entity along it. It does not fall back to straight-line movement when no path exists. navDriveToward(targetX, targetY, speed?, opts?) Car-type CharacterController, NavWorld2D and NavAgent2D for the full vehicle tuning/agent behavior. Follows a path using vehicle steering, lookahead, braking and recovery behavior. Use Pathfinding and Navigation: complete setup for setup, options and examples. Component sub-objects These modules are available only when the named component is attached to the same entity. Accessing a missing component module or misspelling a member produces a clear runtime API error. The generated complete script-module index lists every exposed member and its read/write or method status. TransformAPI this.state Every entity; no Inspector component. Starts at state default . StateAPI and State & messaging this.myTouch Every entity; collider is needed for pointer/finger hit detection. TouchTrackAPI Scene-level module scene.lighting is not attached to this . It exposes scene-wide LightingSettings through the global scene object. When there is no LightingSettings component in the scene, reads use renderer defaults and writes have no effect. See LightingSettingsAPI and LightingSettings .

title: Architecture
description: How Realot Studio separates runtime, editor, standalone runtime, components and systems.
headings: Systems run in an explicit order
content: Runtime / editor / target The distribution follows a hard separation: project/runtime/ is the engine shipped with games; project/editor/ is the development tool; project/player/ is the standalone runtime shell. Runtime must not import editor code; editor may import runtime code. Components are data Components are plain data objects. Rendering, physics, lighting, audio and other behavior live in systems. This keeps scene serialization straightforward and makes the same scene data usable by the editor and standalone runtime. Systems run in an explicit order Order System 1 ControllerSystem 2 PhysicsSystem 3 AnimationSystem 4 SpeechBubbleSystem 5 TextInputSystem 6 JoystickSystem 7 AudioSystem 8 AudioListenerSystem 9 ScriptSystem 10 Late controller work 11 RenderSystem 12 TilemapSystem 13 NavWorldSystem 14 LightingSystem 15 CameraRenderSystem Rendering containers The runtime separates game-content rendering, screen-space UI and late letterbox/pillarbox bars. Debug lines render in the world container. This separation explains why screen-space UI components such as TextRenderer can remain fixed while the world camera moves.

title: Entities & components
description: Understand Realot Studio scene entities, IDs, tags, component composition and runtime cloning.
content: Entity identity An entity has a unique stable ID such as e12 , a human-facing name, a tag, active state, optional hierarchy folder, prefab metadata and a component map. Names and tags are not unique; IDs are. Why IDs matter Use findById(id) when you mean one exact entity. Use name/tag queries when you intentionally want one or many matches. Runtime clones keep unique IDs and expose isClone . Component composition A gameplay actor can combine Transform + SpriteRenderer + Collider2D + Rigidbody2D + Script. A UI button might combine Transform + TextRenderer + Collider2D + Script. There is no requirement that every entity have every component. Runtime cloning Use spawn() or this.spawn() to clone an authored entity. The returned context is the new live entity; onClone() runs for runtime clones before onStart() . js function onUpdate () { if ( input . keyPressed ( "Space" )) { var bullet = spawn ( "Bullet" , { x : this . x , y : this . y }); bullet . rotation = this . rotation ; // configure the clone right after spawning } } // Inside Bullet’s own script: function onClone () { this . tag = "projectile" ; // runs once, before this clone’s onStart() } Destroying entities this.destroy() queues destruction for the end of the frame. onDestroy() runs before removal. Waiting/repeating timers owned by the entity are automatically cancelled when the entity is destroyed.

title: Game loop & scenes
description: Understand frame updates, fixed physics updates and scene transitions.
content: Render-frame lifecycle Hook When it runs onStart() Once before the first onUpdate(). onClone() Once for runtime clones, immediately before onStart(). onUpdate(dt) Every render frame. onClick() On the frame a mouse/finger press targets an entity with a collider. onFixedUpdate(dt) Fixed 60 Hz simulation cadence. onDestroy() Before the entity is removed or the scene ends. Collision & trigger lifecycle Use onCollisionEnter(other) , onCollisionStay(other) and onCollisionExit(other) for physical contacts. onCollision(other) remains an alias for collision-enter behavior. Trigger-only callbacks are onTriggerEnter(other) and onTriggerExit(other) . Scene controls Use scene.current to read the current scene name, scene.load(name) to switch scenes, scene.restart() to restart, and scene.pause() / scene.resume() to freeze gameplay while leaving rendering responsive. js function onTriggerEnter ( other ) { if ( other . name === "Target" ) scene . load ( "Level2" ); } function onUpdate () { if ( input . keyPressed ( "Escape" )) { scene . isPaused ? scene . resume () : scene . pause (); } } Pause semantics During scene.pause() , physics, scripts, animation and audio stop advancing until resume. Rendering stays responsive, which is useful for pause menus and debugging UI.

title: Assets & animation
description: Use sprites, animation clips and audio assets from the editor.
content: Exact control path Imported sprites/audio/scripts/prefabs live in the bottom Project panel. Drag supported assets into the center Scene viewport. For animation, add Sprite Animation in the Inspector, then use the Animation editor window to create clips and import frames. Sprites SpriteRenderer points at an asset key rather than embedding image data in the component. This keeps scene JSON lightweight and lets exported runtime assets remain separate. Animation SpriteAnimation stores clips and current playback state. Scripts can call this.animator.play("Run") , stop playback and inspect current clip/frame information. Audio AudioSource stores the asset key plus playback properties. 3D sources use minDistance for full volume and fade toward silence at maxDistance . AudioListener defines the hearing radius and sound enter/leave callbacks are available to scripts.

title: Complete feature workflows
description: Use these pages when you need to build an entire subsystem, not just understand one property. Each workflow starts with prerequisites and editor locations, then moves through configuration, scripting, testing and troubleshooting.
content: Navigation authoring Create Nav World 2D, configure bounds/cell size, define areas, paint or derive walkable space, add agents, bake/update navigation and debug the result. Navigation from editor to script Complete path from scene setup through NavAgent2D, named area masks/costs, navMoveToward/navDriveToward and runtime troubleshooting. Physics authoring Build colliders, rigidbodies, joints and character controllers, then tune layers, masks, gravity, damping, slopes and one-way platforms. Physics scripting Use Rigidbody2D, Collider2D, raycasts, forces/impulses, collision state and movement APIs from scripts. Lighting, audio and UI Set up lights/shadows, audio sources/listeners, text and interactive UI components with their editor locations and runtime APIs. Tilemaps and tilesets Create tileset data, attach it to a Tilemap, paint, edit tile data and understand the navigation/physics consequences of tile geometry. Assets and animation Import/use sprites, build Sprite Animation clips, choose frames, set playback and connect animation state to scripts. Prefabs Create reusable entity templates, instantiate them, understand overrides, update/revert behavior and runtime spawning. Web/PWA deployment Understand the normal online workflow, standalone web export, PWA behavior and what a deployment must serve. Android APK export Configure the separate build-server workflow and understand what is sent from the browser editor. How to use these guides Start with the prerequisites section. Follow the exact editor path instead of guessing which panel contains a control. Configure the minimum working setup first. Only then add optional tuning such as costs, smoothing, avoidance, shadows, custom input or advanced physics. Run the smallest test scene before integrating the subsystem into a large project. If a result is wrong, use the troubleshooting section before changing unrelated settings.

Android APK export Configure the separate build-server workflow and understand what is sent from the browser editor. How to use these guides Start with the prerequisites section. Follow the exact editor path instead of guessing which panel contains a control. Configure the minimum working setup first. Only then add optional tuning such as costs, smoothing, avoidance, shadows, custom input or advanced physics. Run the smallest test scene before integrating the subsystem into a large project. If a result is wrong, use the troubleshooting section before changing unrelated settings.

title: Components: complete workflow
description: A complete guide to adding, configuring, testing, removing, and scripting components. This page complements each individual component reference; it does not replace the per-component settings tables.
content: 1. Select the entity first Click an entity in the Hierarchy on the left or select it in the Scene viewport. The selected entity's properties appear in the Inspector on the right. 2. Add a component At the bottom of the Inspector click Add Component . A centered Add Component modal opens with a search field and a scrollable list. Type the component name, then click its row. The list excludes components the entity already has. 3. Configure the component After adding it, scroll the Inspector to the new component section. Start with the component's mode/type field if it has one. Changing a mode can expose or hide related settings. Configure required references/assets before tuning numbers. 4. Understand values versus runtime state Serialized authoring settings are saved with the scene. Runtime state fields can change while the game runs and are useful for debugging. Examples include Rigidbody2D velocity/ground state and CharacterController request/state values. 5. Test in Play mode Run the game, observe the result, and inspect the component again when debugging. Change one setting at a time so you can identify which property caused the behavior. 6. Use the dedicated editor tools System Where What it does Sprite Inspector SpriteRenderer section / asset picker Assign the visual asset. Animation SpriteAnimation → Open Animation Window Create and edit clips/frames. Physics Collider/Transform gizmos in Scene viewport Visually inspect/edit geometry. Navigation NavWorld2D + navigation toolbar + Edit → Nav Areas… Author areas, bake/debug navigation, then use NavAgent2D. Tiles Tileset/Tilemap panels Create tile data and paint the map. Stroke Path Stroke Path viewport tool/gizmo Edit path points and inspect serialized path settings. Scripts Script → Create New Script / Load Script… / Open Script Editor Create, attach, edit, and enable scripts. Lighting Light/ShadowCaster gizmos + Inspector Author light geometry and shadow participation. 7. Component combinations that matter Dynamic physics actor: Rigidbody2D + Collider2D; add SpriteRenderer/ShapeRenderer for visuals. Platformer controller: Rigidbody2D + Collider2D + CharacterController; choose Platformer and configure its movement group. Navigation agent: NavWorld2D in the navigation world + NavAgent2D on the moving entity; bake/configure the world before testing agent movement. Animated character: SpriteRenderer + SpriteAnimation, optionally with Rigidbody2D/CharacterController. Interactive UI: the appropriate UI component (TextRenderer, TextInput, Joystick, SpeechBubble, ChatLog) plus Script when behavior is needed. 8. Where to go next Use the component reference for the complete field table, defaults, API members, notes, and examples. Use Navigation: Complete Setup for multi-system navigation. Use Script API Cookbook for complete scripting recipes.

title: Hierarchy & Inspector
description: Organize the current scene and edit entities/components with stable serialized data.
content: Exact control path Select the entity in the left Hierarchy panel or click it in the center Scene view. Its properties appear immediately in the right Inspector . The Add Component button is at the bottom of the Inspector’s component list; use its search field to find a component by name. Hierarchy The Hierarchy shows only entities that belong to the active scene. Entities can also belong to hierarchy folders. The saved scene stores folders separately so folder IDs remain stable across save/load. Inspector The Inspector edits the entity name, tag, active state, component properties and component-specific authoring fields. For many components, the Inspector exposes more authoring fields than the runtime script API intentionally does. Gizmos and shapes Spatial editing uses scene-view gizmos for things such as triangle collider/shape points and other editable geometry. Treat these as authoring controls; scripts should use the documented component APIs instead of manipulating editor gizmo state.

title: Lighting, audio & UI
description: Build atmospheric scenes, sound behavior and responsive UI with Realot Studio components.
content: Exact control path Create lights from GameObject → Light or add Light/Audio/UI components through Inspector → Add Component . Screen-space UI entities can also be created directly from the top UI menu. Lighting Lights support Directional, Point, Spot, Area, GodRays and Freeform types. LightingSettings controls scene-wide shadow quality, ambient darkness and visible glow strength. ShadowCaster controls per-entity shadow geometry and softness. Shadow quality ShadowMode quad is the cheaper analytic mode. raymarch enables per-pixel ray-marched occlusion; raymarchSteps controls accuracy/cost and is clamped to 1-200. UI TextRenderer can be screen-space, while SpeechBubble, ChatLog, TextInput and Joystick provide higher-level UI behaviors. TextInput exposes justSubmitted ; Joystick exposes normalized x/y input and engagement state. Audio listeners AudioSource can be 3D distance-attenuated. AudioListener receives hearing-area transitions that map to onHearSound(source) and onLoseSound(source) .

title: Navigation authoring
description: Bake 2D navigation with NavWorld2D and configure NavAgent2D.
content: Exact control path Create the shared nav grid with GameObject → 2D Object → Nav World 2D . Then the top toolbar exposes U walkable, I blocked and O area paint tools. Brush −/+ controls sit directly beside those nav tools. Named areas are configured at Edit → Nav Areas… . NavWorld2D A NavWorld2D defines world bounds, cell size and authored/baked cell data. It supports 16 navigation areas, per-area costs, optional diagonal traversal and optional dynamic rebuilding. Agents NavAgent2D adds radius, speed, acceleration/deceleration, stopping distance, automatic repathing and avoidance. Vehicle-oriented settings are available for car-style navigation/steering. Script access Scripts use the global nav module: nav.findPath() , nav.isWalkable() and nav.bake() . A NavAgent exposes its live currentPath and currentPathIndex as read-only script state. Pathfinding behavior Path endpoints are snapped to the nearest walkable cell. Returned waypoints are world-space points with straight runs merged, but they are not geometrically smoothed.

title: Physics authoring
description: Configure rigid bodies, colliders, joints, layers and one-way platforms.
content: Exact control path Physics components are added from Inspector → Add Component (Rigidbody 2D, Collider 2D, Joint 2D, Movement Type). Global named physics layer slots are edited at Edit → Physics Layers… . Rigid bodies Body type Typical responsibility Dynamic Physics solver controls movement; scripts apply forces/impulses or read/write velocity. Kinematic Scripts/controllers request movement; collision resolution produces contact state. Static Fixed world geometry; no dynamic motion. Colliders Collider2D supports Box, Circle, Capsule and Triangle shapes. You can enable triggers, one-way platforms, friction/restitution, density, offsets and 16-layer collision filtering. Collision layers Each collider belongs to one layer (0-15) and exposes a 16-bit mask of layers it can interact with. A raycast can use physics.layer(…) to build the same mask model for query filtering. Joints Joint2D supports Fixed, Revolute, Prismatic, Rope and Spring. Rope and Spring use multi-segment chains for visual/physical behavior and expose anchors, length, stiffness/damping and optional motors/limits. One-way platforms Direction matters A one-way platform is a Collider2D with isOneWayPlatform = true . The physics system distinguishes pass-through movement from the blocking direction, so the behavior should be tested with the body moving from both sides.

title: Prefab workflow
description: Create, place, edit, update, revert and unpack Realot Studio prefabs with the exact editor controls involved.
content: What a prefab is In Realot Studio a prefab is a reusable one-entity template. Instances keep a prefabId and track field-level overrides. Updating a prefab can propagate the canonical data to other instances. Create a prefab Select an entity in the Scene viewport or Hierarchy. In the right Inspector, use the small prefab/box action next to the entity name. The engine creates a prefab from that entity and links the source entity to it. Place an instance Use the bottom Project panel → Prefabs folder. Drag a prefab asset into the center Scene viewport. The editor instantiates the template and places the new instance in the scene. Edit an instance Change component values normally in the Inspector. Realot Studio records changed fields as prefab overrides for that instance. Update the prefab When an instance is selected, the Inspector shows a blue Prefab strip. Optional Update Transform checkboxes control whether Position, Rotation, and Scale should also propagate to other instances. Click Update Prefab to make this instance the new canonical template. Revert / Unpack Inspector control Effect Revert Prefab Discard the instance’s overrides and re-sync its values from the prefab. Unpack Prefab Detach this instance while keeping its current values. Future prefab updates no longer reach it. Delete a prefab asset Bottom Project → Prefabs. Use the asset delete control. Existing objects keep their current data but are no longer linked to the deleted prefab. Important implementation fact Prefab data is stored in the project’s prefabs.json catalogue and is included by Save Project/import/export flows.

title: Scenes & projects
description: Save, load, switch, duplicate and serialize Realot Studio scenes and project manifests.
content: Exact control path Project-level scene/file operations are in the bottom Project panel. Scene creation uses Project → Scenes → New Scene ; Save Project and Load Project are in the top File menu. The autosave indicator/action is also exposed through File → Save Now / Saved . Scene workflow The Scene Manager supports creating, saving, switching, renaming, duplicating and deleting scenes. The last remaining scene cannot be deleted. Project compatibility The project manifest stores compatibility metadata. When a project created by a newer engine build is opened in an older build, the editor can show a compatibility warning. This information belongs to the saved project and does not create versioned documentation pages or download releases. Recommended practice Keep source projects with explicit scene names, tags and stable IDs. Keep backups of important project archives before opening them in a different engine build, especially when compatibility warnings appear. Save and reopen a project Choose File → Save Project in the editor to download a .realot project file. To reopen it by double-clicking, install Realot Hub as a PWA in a desktop browser that supports file handling. Double-click the .realot file in your file manager; the installed Realot app opens the project in the editor. Realot can ask permission to save future changes back to the same file. If your browser does not support PWA file handling, use File → Load Project inside the editor.

title: Editor settings and configuration
description: Complete reference for the editor menus, panel visibility, physics layers, navigation areas, Inspector notes, saving preferences and performance defaults.
content: Where the settings are Realot Studio does not currently have one large Settings window. Options are placed beside the editor feature they control: use File for project storage and export, Edit for physics and navigation labels, and Window for panel visibility. Component-specific settings live in the Inspector and are documented on each component reference page . File menu Menu item What it does Availability / notes Save Now / Saved Immediately saves the open Hub project to its browser autosave storage. The label shows whether there are unsaved changes. Shown when the project was opened with a Hub autosave slot. Save Project Downloads a portable .realot project archive. When editing a supported file handle, the label can become Save to [filename] . Available for project export to a local file. Auto-update file: ON / OFF Controls whether changes are automatically written back to the opened project file. title: Tilemaps & tilesets
description: Author sparse tile grids and 16-role autotile tilesets.
content: Exact control path Create a reusable tileset via GameObject → 2D Object → Tileset and the tile grid via GameObject → 2D Object → Tilemap . Once present, T selects tile painting and Y selects erase. The Tileset Editor exposes the 4×4 role grid and import actions. Tileset authoring The editor can take one image and auto-slice it into a 4×4 role grid, or accept up to 16 separate role images. The stored result is sixteen role-to-sprite-key mappings. The 16 roles The canonical order is cornerTL, edgeT, cornerTR, stubT, edgeL, center, edgeR, lineV, cornerBL, edgeB, cornerBR, stubB, stubL, lineH, stubR, single . Tilemap data A Tilemap references a Tileset by entity ID and stores a sparse set of filled cells keyed as col,row . The runtime computes the visual tile role from orthogonal neighbors; it does not store the final role per cell. Scripting No direct Tilemap script module Tilemap/Tileset are editor/scene-data components. There is currently no documented this.tilemap runtime API.

title: Export an Android APK
description: Build an Android APK directly from the Realot Studio Export window. The current editor allows three APK exports in a rolling 14-day period.
headings: When an export does not finish
content: One simple flow Click Export , choose Android APK , and let Realot build the file. There is no separate setup wizard or need to export HTML5 first. Steps Open the game project in Realot Studio. Click Export in the editor toolbar. You can also use File → Export… . In the Export Game window, choose Android APK . Wait for the build to finish. Realot downloads the finished .apk file to your device. The game title is filled in from the project name and can be changed before exporting. Choosing a custom favicon is optional. Those are the only optional details shown in the export form; you do not need Android Studio, Gradle, the Android SDK or a separate web export. APK export limit The current editor allows 3 APK exports in a rolling 14-day period . The Export window shows how many of the three remain and explains when an export becomes available again. The window is rolling: an export becomes available again 14 days after the corresponding counted export, rather than all three resetting on one calendar date. An export is counted after the build service accepts the job. A failed or cancelled build gives that export back. HTML5 and PWA exports are not limited by the APK quota. Quota detail for support and AI tools The supplied browser client records the rolling quota in this browser's local storage. It is therefore a per-browser client allowance, not an account-based counter. The build service should enforce its own server-side usage limits; clearing browser data is not a supported way to manage exports. What the APK contains The current Android option produces a debug-signed APK intended for testing and direct installation on an Android device. It is not a Play Store production-signed release. The Android build service is needed to create the APK; the downloaded game does not need to contact that service while it is running. When an export does not finish Read the message shown in the Export window. If the service is waking up or temporarily unavailable, try again later. A failed or cancelled build returns the consumed export allowance. If the same error keeps happening, copy the message from the export window and include it when reporting the issue. Other export formats HTML5: creates a standalone web game you can host as a static site. PWA: creates the web game plus an installable manifest and service worker for offline use. Desktop (Windows/Mac/Linux): listed in the format picker as coming soon in the supplied engine build. For the other formats, see HTML5 and PWA export or the Export window reference .

title: Export window reference
description: Understand the game title, favicon, export formats, build progress and Android APK quota.
headings: Build an APK from a web export
content: Open the Export window from File → Export… or the toolbar's Export button. Game details Field Behavior Game title Up to 80 characters; defaults to the project name. Used for the exported page title and Android app name. Favicon Optional image selected in the Export window. It is used as the exported web game's icon and, where supported by the APK wrapper, the Android launcher icon. Format cards Card Status Output HTML5 Available Standalone static game package. PWA Available HTML5 package plus manifest and service worker. Desktop (Windows/Mac/Linux) Coming soon / disabled Not generated by the current Export window. Android APK Available A debug-signed APK built by the configured remote service. Browser-side web packaging HTML5/PWA packaging runs in the browser. The exporter includes the game runtime and referenced assets, not the editor. When asset optimization is supported by the browser, images/audio may be re-encoded and checked before inclusion. The result is a downloadable ZIP. Use a local HTTP server or static host to run it; direct file:// opening is not supported. Android APK workflow The Android card uses the built-in service configured for this Realot deployment. The editor prepares the standalone game ZIP, requests or renews a temporary build token, uploads the ZIP, polls the job and downloads the APK. You do not add a custom build server or paste an API key into the Export window. The card shows the service connection state and the remaining APK export allowance. The current client-side allowance is 3 accepted builds in a rolling 14-day window per browser ; the authoritative service may apply additional server-side limits. Progress and cancellation While an APK is building, the Export window displays progress and offers Cancel build . The editor polls the job approximately every 2.5 seconds and uses a 10-minute client timeout. Cancelling or leaving the editor signals cancellation to the service when possible. HTML5 and PWA packaging occurs locally in the browser. Build an APK from a web export After an HTML5 or PWA export, the result screen can offer Build APK from this HTML5/PWA export . This sends the exact web ZIP already created, so the game package does not need to be rebuilt.

title: HTML5 and PWA export
description: Create a standalone HTML5 game or a PWA with a manifest and service worker.
content: HTML5 HTML5 export produces a standalone static game package. The ZIP contains an index.html entry point, game code, the standalone runtime and the assets required by the project. It does not include the editor or Hub. PWA PWA export adds a web app manifest and service worker to the same standalone game package. The browser can offer installation and offline caching when the deployment meets the browser's PWA requirements. Hosting checklist Extract the ZIP and keep the entry point, runtime and referenced assets together. Serve the package over HTTP(S); do not rely on opening index.html directly with file:// . Use HTTPS on a public deployment when browser security rules or PWA installation require a secure origin. Test the exported game independently of the editor before sharing it.

title: Build your first game
description: A practical first-game path using entities, components and a simple script.
headings: 3. Add physics when you need it
content: 1. Start with a scene Create a scene and add an entity. The editor stores scene state as JSON-compatible data: entities have IDs, names, tags, active state, optional hierarchy folders/prefab metadata, and a component map. 2. Add a visual Attach a SpriteRenderer and assign a sprite asset, or use a ShapeRenderer when you want a procedural primitive. Add a Camera and mark one camera as the main camera. 3. Add physics when you need it A typical physics actor uses a Rigidbody2D plus a Collider2D . Choose Dynamic, Kinematic or Static based on who is responsible for movement. 4. Add a Script component Put a script on the entity and define lifecycle functions. Realot Studio calls onStart() once and onUpdate(dt) every render frame. js function onStart () { this . speed = 220 ; } function onUpdate ( dt ) { if ( input . keyDown ( "ArrowRight" )) { this . x += this . speed * dt ; } if ( input . keyDown ( "ArrowLeft" )) { this . x -= this . speed * dt ; } } 5. Prefer frame-rate-independent movement Use time.deltaTime (or the dt lifecycle argument) when movement is expressed in units per second. Keep physics-step work in onFixedUpdate(dt) when the logic should track the fixed simulation cadence. 6. Run, iterate, export Use the editor’s Play flow to test, inspect the Debug HUD when diagnosing runtime behavior, then use Export for HTML5, PWA or Android APK.

title: The Realot Hub
description: Use Projects to create and reopen games, and Learn to open the built-in guide.
headings: Install the Hub as an app
content: Overview The Hub is the Realot Studio home screen. It is the starting point for opening projects, creating a new game from a template, and opening the built-in learning material. The current Hub has two views: Projects and Learn . View What it does Projects Shows your saved project cards. Start with a template, create a blank project, search/sort your projects, switch between grid and list layouts, or reopen a recent project. Learn Opens the Hub's learning area. The built-in quick guide is part of the engine distribution and can be cached for offline access. Starter templates The current template gallery includes: Template Starting point Blank Canvas An empty project for custom 2D scenes and logic. Platformer Kit A platformer starter with a kinematic character controller and one-way platforms. Top-Down A top-down starter with a player, NPCs, collectibles and a dungeon scene. Flappy Bird A flap-to-fly starter with scoring and a simple game-state flow. Sky Jumper An endless jumping starter with platforms, stars and a following camera. Physics Sandbox A scene for experimenting with Rapier2D bodies, colliders and joints. Install the Hub as an app Realot is a web application. On browsers and deployments that support installation, the title bar can show an Install app action when the browser confirms the site is installable. Installation creates an app-like shortcut; it does not download a separate engine release. The service worker can cache the Hub, editor and runtime for supported offline use. Updates are published to the hosted site. When the browser is online, reload the site to receive the current published files. An installed PWA may continue using cached files while offline and will need to reconnect to refresh them. Project files File → Save Project downloads your project as a .realot file. This is Realot Studio's portable project format and includes the scenes, assets, prefabs, tags, navigation-area names and scripts needed to continue editing the game. Open a project from your computer: install Realot Hub as a PWA in a supported desktop browser. Then double-click a downloaded .realot file in your file manager. The operating system opens the installed Realot app, and Realot loads that project in the editor. When asked, you can allow Realot to keep saving changes back to that same file. This file-opening behavior requires an installed PWA and browser/operating-system support for web-app file handling; if that option is unavailable, open the editor and use File → Load Project .

title: Use Realot Studio
description: Realot Studio is a browser-based engine. Open the hosted site; local hosting is optional.
content: Normal use: open the website No engine installer is required Realot Studio runs as a browser application. Open the hosted Realot site in a modern browser and use the Hub to create or open a project. The editor and runtime are delivered as web files; you do not need to download a separate engine installer to use the hosted version. When the engine owner publishes an update to the hosted site, the new files are available from the same website address. A normal page reload while online retrieves the published files. A previously installed PWA can continue using cached assets offline until it reconnects and refreshes. Optional browser installation On a supported browser and deployment, choose the Hub's Install app action or use the browser's own install option. This adds an app-like launcher entry. It is still the same web application and does not create a separate downloadable engine release. Optional: host the engine yourself The supplied engine project is a static web application. To preview a local copy or publish your own deployment, serve the project folder over HTTP(S). For a quick local preview, run this command from the folder containing the engine files: shell python3 -m http.server 5000 Then open http://localhost:5000/ . Do not open the main HTML file directly with file:// ; browser module, fetch and WebAssembly loading require an HTTP origin. Browser requirements A modern browser with JavaScript modules and WebAssembly. Canvas/WebGL support for the renderer. Browser storage for project data and preferences. HTTPS for production deployments that need secure browser APIs or PWA installation (localhost is treated as secure for development). Android APK export Android APK export is separate from normal browser use. Realot packages the game in the browser and sends the standalone web export to the configured Android build service. The editor does not run Android Studio, Gradle or an Android SDK locally. See Android APK export for the current workflow.

title: Scripting quickstart
description: Learn the Realot Studio JavaScript scripting model in one page.
headings: The two layers of the API
content: Script shape Realot Studio scripts are plain JavaScript functions executed by the ScriptSystem. You do not create a class instance yourself. The engine binds the entity context to this . js function onStart () { this . health = 100 ; } function onUpdate ( dt ) { this . x += 100 * dt ; } The two layers of the API Layer Examples Use when Entity context ( this ) this.x , this.sprite , this.rigidbody , this.destroy() You are acting on the current entity. Globals findFirst() , scene.load() , physics.raycast() , input.keyDown() You need scene-wide services or another entity. Common component shortcuts When a component exists on the entity, the corresponding module is exposed on this : this.sprite , this.shape , this.text , this.rigidbody , this.controller , this.animator , this.camera , this.audio , this.collider , this.joint , this.navAgent , this.light , this.shadowCaster , this.strokePath , and more. Discoverability The editor’s script autocomplete is sourced from the same public API lists documented here. A good rule for generated code is: use documented globals and component modules; do not reach into internal runtime systems or editor modules.

title: Realot Studio documentation
description: Source-aligned documentation for Realot Studio: editor workflows, scripting API, components, physics, navigation and export.
content: What is Realot Studio? A browser-based 2D game engine with a visual editor, JavaScript gameplay scripting, PixiJS rendering and Rapier2D physics. The hosted engine is updated by publishing its web files; users do not need a separate engine installer. Start here Open Realot Studio Use the hosted editor or serve the static distribution yourself. Build your first game Entities, components and a first script in a few steps. Scripting quickstart onStart, onUpdate, this and the component modules. Editor controls Exact menu paths, panels and keyboard shortcuts. Browse by topic Get started Run the editor, build a first game and learn the scripting model. 5 pages Concepts Architecture, the entity–component model, the game loop and coordinates. 4 pages Editor Every panel, menu path, shortcut and authoring workflow. 13 pages Scripting Lifecycle, globals, input, physics, navigation, saving and debugging. 18 pages API reference Component fields, script members, option shapes and prerequisites. 6 pages Export & deploy HTML5, installable PWA and Android APK builds. 4 pages Reference Tuning rules, scene and project formats, live updates and source map. 8 pages AI & machine access llms.txt, Markdown twins, JSON catalogs and guidance for assistants. 3 pages Component reference 25 components, each documented with serialized fields, defaults, script API and editor location. Transform Position, rotation and scale. Every spatial entity uses a Transform. SpriteRenderer Draw a 2D texture sprite for an entity. ShapeRenderer Draw a procedural 2D shape without requiring a sprite asset. TextRenderer Render text either in world space or as screen-space UI. StrokePath A variable-thickness strip along placed points — rivers, cables, roads, conveyor belts or walls — with flat color or… SpeechBubble Speech bubble UI attached to an entity, useful for dialogue and NPC callouts. ChatLog Scrollable-style conversation log component for UI dialogue. TextInput Interactive text input control driven by the runtime UI system. Joystick Virtual touch joystick for mobile and pointer-driven control schemes. Rigidbody2D 2D physics body backed by the engine physics runtime. Dynamic, Kinematic and Static bodies have different script… Collider2D Physics collision shape and contact filtering. A Collider2D is also required for accurate pointer/touch hit tests. Joint2D Connect physics bodies with Fixed, Revolute, Prismatic, Rope or Spring constraints. CharacterController High-level movement modes: Character Controller, Platformer, Top-Down, Car, Follow, Patrol and Free. SpriteAnimation Sprite-sheet/clip animation state on a SpriteRenderer. Camera Orthographic 2D camera with reference resolutions, responsive scaling, follow, shake and optional pseudo-3D sprite… AudioSource Play a local audio asset, optionally with distance-based 3D attenuation. AudioListener Defines the hearing area for 3D audio and drives audio enter/leave callbacks. Light 2D light source supporting Directional, Point, Spot, Area, GodRays and Freeform light shapes. ShadowCaster Marks an entity as a shadow occluder for the lighting system. LightingSettings Scene-wide lighting quality and mood controls. Attach to one entity; the lighting system reads it scene-wide. NavAgent2D Per-agent navigation settings and current path state for NavWorld2D pathfinding. NavWorld2D Shared navigation world for baked or dynamic 2D pathfinding, with 16 navigation areas. Tileset Defines a reusable 16-role autotile set. The editor can auto-slice one image or accept separate role images. Tilemap Sparse painted tile grid that references a Tileset entity by ID. Script Script component holding a script name, source and enabled state. For automated systems Every page is complete static HTML with a Markdown twin (same URL, .md ). Machine entry points: llms.txt , llms-full.txt (all documentation in one file), search-index.json , api/index.json , sitemap.xml and robots.txt . See AI & crawlers .
