title: AI Bridge: connect an AI assistant
description: Connect an MCP-compatible AI app to the open Realot Studio editor using the built-in shared relay, with optional self-hosting, read-only mode and a complete source-derived tool catalog.
headings: About the included local MCP companion source
content: Built in and ready to use Realot Studio includes a shared relay address. Most users do not need to install Node.js, configure a local server, create a Cloudflare account or deploy anything. Open AI Bridge, copy the private link into an AI app that supports remote MCP connectors, and press Connect in Realot. Connect your AI assistant Open your project in Realot Studio and click AI Bridge in the editor. Click Copy link in the panel. In your AI app, open its connector or MCP-server settings. Add a remote MCP server or custom connector , paste the copied link, and name it Realot . The exact menu name depends on the AI app. Return to Realot and click Connect . The panel should show Connected . Ask the AI to inspect the open project before asking it to make changes. The copied link contains a private secret key. Treat it like a password: anyone who has the link may be able to use the tools exposed by your open editor. Do not post it in public messages or commit it to a project repository. AI Bridge panel options Option What it does Copy link Copies the private remote MCP connector URL for this editor. Connect / Disconnect Starts or closes the editor's connection to the relay. The editor must remain open while the AI works on the live project. Read-only Blocks tools that change the project. The AI can inspect the editor but cannot perform supported edit operations while this is enabled. Connect automatically when the editor opens Remembers the preference and reconnects on a later editor launch when a private key is already configured. Make a new private link Creates a new secret key and invalidates the old link. Add the new link to your AI app; the old connector URL will no longer authenticate. Need more AI time? → click here to host it Opens Cloudflare's deployment flow for an optional personal copy of the relay. This is not needed for the built-in shared relay. Use it / Default Use it switches to the relay URL you supplied and refreshes the connector link. Default switches back to Realot's built-in shared relay. Re-copy the connector link after changing relay addresses. Shared relay time allowance The built-in shared relay includes 30 minutes of active AI work in each 24-hour usage window . Time is counted while a tool call is running and for up to 20 seconds between calls. Being connected while the AI is idle does not use the allowance. The panel shows the remaining time and the reset countdown. The usage record is kept in this browser's local storage. It is a client-side allowance display and should not be treated as an account-wide quota or a tamper-proof billing record. Hosting your own relay removes the shared-relay active-time limit; Cloudflare account usage and service terms may still apply. Optional: host a personal relay Most users should stay on the built-in relay. Hosting your own is an advanced option for users who want to avoid the shared-relay time allowance or operate their own relay endpoint. In the AI Bridge panel, select click here to host it . Realot opens the Cloudflare deployment page for the relay source repository. Complete Cloudflare's deployment and copy the HTTPS address ending in .workers.dev . Paste that address into the relay field in the AI Bridge panel and click Use it . Click Copy link again and replace the old Realot connector URL in your AI app. Connect from the editor. To return to the shared relay, click Default , copy the refreshed link, and update the connector in your AI app. A personal relay has no Realot active-AI-minutes cap, but you are responsible for its deployment, availability and Cloudflare account. What the AI can do The built-in relay currently exposes 80 MCP tools . They allow an AI app to inspect editor state, scenes and entities; create and modify entities and components; read, write and attach scripts; start or pause play mode; inspect the Console and capture a screenshot; manage assets and chunked uploads; edit animation clips and frames; manage tilesets and tilemaps; paint navigation cells and configure navigation and physics layers; manage tags, folders, prefabs and scenes; save or export project data; and control editor panels and tools. The tables below list every hosted tool name and its input fields. Fields shown in bold are required. Full JSON input schemas—including exact types, constraints and additional properties—are published in the machine-readable API catalog under aiBridge.sharedRelayTools . Complete hosted MCP tool catalog Project and scene inspection Tool What it does get_editor_state Inputs: none Overview of the open Realot editor: project name, whether the game is playing, selected entity ids, entity count, available component types. list_entities Inputs: limit : integer List every entity in the current scene (id, name, tag, active, component types, x/y position). get_entity Inputs: id : string (required) Full data of one entity: all components with every property. list_scenes Inputs: none List every scene in the project and which one is active. Entities and components Tool What it does create_entity Inputs: name : string (required) ; x : number; y : number; tag : string; components : object Create an entity. 'components' maps a component type (e.g. SpriteRenderer, Collider2D, Rigidbody2D, Script) to its properties. A Transform is always added. Undoable with undo. Values are validated: wrong types, unknown properties, invalid enum values (e.g. Light.type), out-of-range numbers, bad hex colors and values the engine would silently clamp are rejected with a message listing every problem and the allowed values; nothing is changed on error. update_component Inputs: id : string (required) ; type : string (required) ; props : object (required) Change properties of an existing component on an entity (only properties the component already has). Use get_entity first to see them. Values are validated: wrong types, unknown properties, invalid enum values (e.g. Light.type), out-of-range numbers, bad hex colors and values the engine would silently clamp are rejected with a message listing every problem and the allowed values; nothing is changed on error. add_component Inputs: id : string (required) ; type : string (required) ; props : object Add a component to an entity. Values are validated: wrong types, unknown properties, invalid enum values (e.g. Light.type), out-of-range numbers, bad hex colors and values the engine would silently clamp are rejected with a message listing every problem and the allowed values; nothing is changed on error. remove_component Inputs: id : string (required) ; type : string (required) Remove a component (not Transform) from an entity. delete_entities Inputs: ids : array (required) Delete entities by id (same as pressing Delete in the editor). Undoable. select_entities Inputs: ids : array (required) Select entities in the editor so the user sees them in the Inspector. update_entity Inputs: id : string (required) ; patch : object (required) Rename an entity or change its tag, active flag, or hierarchy folder. Use update_component for Transform and other components. create_scene Inputs: name : string; switch : boolean Create a new scene (with a Main Camera). Switches to it unless switch=false. switch_scene Inputs: scene_id : string (required) Make another scene the active one in the editor. rename_scene Inputs: scene_id : string (required) ; name : string (required) Rename a scene. delete_scene Inputs: scene_id : string (required) ; confirm : boolean Delete a scene. Cannot be undone, so the first call only reports what would be deleted; repeat with confirm=true. A project must keep one scene. duplicate_scene Inputs: scene_id : string (required) Duplicate a scene (deep copy) and add it to the project. Does not switch to it. Scripts, play mode and diagnostics Tool What it does list_scripts Inputs: none Names of all scripts in the project. get_script Inputs: name : string (required) Source code of a script. write_script Inputs: name : string (required) ; source : string (required) Create or overwrite a script's source code. Entities already using this script get the new code too. Reports syntax errors. attach_script Inputs: id : string (required) ; scriptName : string (required) Attach an existing script to an entity (adds a Script component). set_playing Inputs: playing : boolean (required) Start or stop play mode (opens the game in the play window). get_console Inputs: limit : integer Recent editor/play console lines (logs, warnings, script errors). screenshot Inputs: none Image of the scene viewport as the user sees it. undo Inputs: none Undo the last editor change. redo Inputs: none Redo the last undone change. delete_script Inputs: name : string (required) ; confirm : boolean Delete a script from the project and clear it from objects using it. Cannot be undone, so the first call reports usage; repeat with confirm=true. set_script_enabled Inputs: id : string (required) ; enabled : boolean (required) Enable or disable the Script component on an entity without removing it. set_paused Inputs: paused : boolean (required) Pause or resume the running game. The game must be playing (see set_playing). Assets and uploads Tool What it does list_assets Inputs: kind : string [all, sprite, animation, frame, tile, audio]; query : string; limit : integer List imported images and audio without returning binary data, grouped like the editor's Project folders: Sprites, Animation Clips (uploaded animation frames) and Tiles (tileset images), plus Audio. Use the keys in SpriteRenderer, AudioSource, animation clips, and tilesets. begin_asset_upload Inputs: file_name : string (required) ; mime_type : string (required) ; size_bytes : integer (required) ; purpose : string [sprite, audio, animation-image, animation-zip, animation-gif, animation-sheet, tileset-sheet, tileset-tile, frame-asset, tile-asset, project-zip] (required) ; entity_id : string; clip_id : string; tileset_entity_id : string; role : string; grid_cols : integer; grid_rows : integer; group : string Start uploading a custom asset: a sprite, audio file, animation source, tileset image, or a loose image for the Animation Clips folder (purpose 'frame-asset') or Tiles folder (purpose 'tile-asset'). Then send sequential base64 chunks with append_asset_upload_chunk and finish with complete_asset_upload. The editor must be open and connected. Maximum 20 MiB per file. Purpose 'project-zip' (a .realot project, max 20 MiB) REPLACES the entire open project and asks the person at the editor to confirm. Animation uploads land in the Animation Clips folder; tileset uploads land in the Tiles folder. append_asset_upload_chunk Inputs: upload_id : string (required) ; chunk_index : integer (required) ; chunk_base64 : string (required) Send one base64-encoded binary chunk for an active asset upload. Chunks must be independent base64 strings, sequential from index 0. Use the chunk size returned by begin_asset_upload; retrying the same index and data is safe. complete_asset_upload Inputs: upload_id : string (required) Validate and import all received bytes using the editor's native import pipeline. Call only after every chunk has been accepted. cancel_asset_upload Inputs: upload_id : string (required) Discard a staged upload before it is imported. rename_asset Inputs: key : string (required) ; kind : string [sprite, frame, animation, tile, audio] (required) ; name : string (required) Rename an imported sprite, animation frame, tile or audio asset while preserving its key and references. delete_asset Inputs: key : string (required) ; kind : string [sprite, frame, animation, tile, audio] (required) ; confirm : boolean Delete an imported asset. If the asset is referenced by scenes or prefabs, the first call reports those references; set confirm=true only when it is acceptable to leave them unresolved. slice_asset_into_tileset Inputs: entity_id : string (required) ; asset_key : string (required) Cut one existing project image (for example an uploaded sprite) into a 4x4 grid and fill all 16 Tileset slots with the pieces. The pieces are saved in the Tiles folder under the tileset's name. Undoable. Animation Tool What it does list_animations Inputs: none List animation clips and ordered frame keys for every entity in the active scene. create_animation_clip Inputs: entity_id : string (required) ; name : string; fps : number; loop : boolean Create an empty animation clip on an entity, adding SpriteAnimation if needed, and open it in the animation editor. update_animation_clip Inputs: entity_id : string (required) ; clip_id : string (required) ; fields : object (required) Change an animation clip name, frame rate, loop setting, or collider override. Set collider_override to null to remove the override. delete_animation_clip Inputs: entity_id : string (required) ; clip_id : string (required) Delete one animation clip from its entity. The remaining clips and frames are preserved. move_animation_frame Inputs: entity_id : string (required) ; clip_id : string (required) ; from_index : integer (required) ; to_index : integer (required) Reorder an animation frame by moving it from one zero-based position to another. delete_animation_frame Inputs: entity_id : string (required) ; clip_id : string (required) ; frame_index : integer (required) Remove one zero-based frame position from an animation clip without deleting the underlying imported asset. add_animation_frames Inputs: entity_id : string (required) ; clip_id : string (required) ; asset_keys : array (required) ; index : integer Add images that are already in the project (sprites, Animation Clips frames, or Tiles) to an animation clip as frames. Use list_assets for keys and list_animations for entity/clip ids. Optional index inserts at that position instead of appending. Undoable. Tilesets and tilemaps Tool What it does list_tilesets Inputs: none List tilesets, tile dimensions, and sprite keys assigned to each role. update_tileset Inputs: entity_id : string (required) ; patch : object (required) Edit a tileset name, tile dimensions, or selected role-to-sprite assignments. Safe and reliable use Start with project inspection. Ask the AI to identify the active scene, selected objects and relevant components before it edits anything. Use Read-only when you only want explanations or an audit. Ask the AI to make a small change first, then inspect the result in the editor and test it in Play mode. Use undo for supported scene edits. Do not assume every operation—especially script writes, project-file operations or scene-list changes—can be reversed in the same way. Save a project backup before large edits. Review generated JavaScript. Project scripts execute as browser page code and are not an isolated security sandbox. Do not run untrusted scripts or import project archives from sources you do not trust. Tool results may contain project names, scenes, scripts, assets and Console output. These are sent to the connected AI app; use an AI provider you trust and avoid connecting projects containing secrets or private data. Disconnect when finished and keep the private connector URL secret. Use Make a new private link if you think the link has been exposed. About the included local MCP companion source The engine archive also contains a Node.js stdio companion under mcp-bridge/ and an editor integration module under project/editor/mcp/EditorBridge.js . In this supplied build, that editor integration's installer is not called by the editor startup path. The local companion is therefore not a supported, ready-to-connect alternative in the packaged editor. Use the built-in shared relay described above. Developers who want a local stdio integration must first wire and test the companion against the editor; its 23 local tool definitions are not the same interface as the 80 tools exposed by the live shared relay. For AI clients and coding agents Start with For AI assistants & LLMs , then read the script-module reference and global runtime API when generating game scripts. AI Bridge tools edit the editor; script APIs run inside the game. They are different interfaces.

x: Built in and ready to use Realot Studio includes a shared relay address. Most users do not need to install Node.js, configure a local server, create a Cloudflare account or deploy anything. Open AI Bridge, copy the private link into an AI app that supports remote MCP connectors, and press Connect in Realot. Connect your AI assistant Open your project in Realot Studio and click AI Bridge in the editor. Click Copy link in the panel. In your AI app, open its connector or MCP-server settings. Add a remote MCP server or custom connector , paste the copied link, and name it Realot . The exact menu name depends on the AI app. Return to Realot and click Connect . The panel should show Connected . Ask the AI to inspect the open project before asking it to make changes. The copied link contains a private secret key. Treat it like a password: anyone who has the link may be able to use the tools exposed by your open editor. Do not post it in public messages or commit it to a project repository. AI Bridge panel options Option What it does Copy link Copies the private remote MCP connector URL for this editor. Connect / Disconnect Starts or closes the editor's connection to the relay. The editor must remain open while the AI works on the live project. Read-only Blocks tools that change the project. The AI can inspect the editor but cannot perform supported edit operations while this is enabled. Connect automatically when the editor opens Remembers the preference and reconnects on a later editor launch when a private key is already configured. Make a new private link Creates a new secret key and invalidates the old link. Add the new link to your AI app; the old connector URL will no longer authenticate. Need more AI time? → click here to host it Opens Cloudflare's deployment flow for an optional personal copy of the relay. This is not needed for the built-in shared relay. Use it / Default Use it switches to the relay URL you supplied and refreshes the connector link. Default switches back to Realot's built-in shared relay. Re-copy the connector link after changing relay addresses. Shared relay time allowance The built-in shared relay includes 30 minutes of active AI work in each 24-hour usage window . Time is counted while a tool call is running and for up to 20 seconds between calls. Being connected while the AI is idle does not use the allowance. The panel shows the remaining time and the reset countdown. The usage record is kept in this browser's local storage. It is a client-side allowance display and should not be treated as an account-wide quota or a tamper-proof billing record. Hosting your own relay removes the shared-relay active-time limit; Cloudflare account usage and service terms may still apply. Optional: host a personal relay Most users should stay on the built-in relay. Hosting your own is an advanced option for users who want to avoid the shared-relay time allowance or operate their own relay endpoint. In the AI Bridge panel, select click here to host it . Realot opens the Cloudflare deployment page for the relay source repository. Complete Cloudflare's deployment and copy the HTTPS address ending in .workers.dev . Paste that address into the relay field in the AI Bridge panel and click Use it . Click Copy link again and replace the old Realot connector URL in your AI app. Connect from the editor. To return to the shared relay, click Default , copy the refreshed link, and update the connector in your AI app. A personal relay has no Realot active-AI-minutes cap, but you are responsible for its deployment, availability and Cloudflare account. What the AI can do The built-in relay currently exposes 80 MCP tools . They allow an AI app to inspect editor state, scenes and entities; create and modify entities and components; read, write and attach scripts; start or pause play mode; inspect the Console and capture a screenshot; manage assets and chunked uploads; edit animation clips and frames; manage tilesets and tilemaps; paint navigation cells and configure navigation and physics layers; manage tags, folders, prefabs and scenes; save or export project data; and control editor panels and tools. The tables below list every hosted tool name and its input fields. Fields shown in bold are required. Full JSON input schemas—including exact types, constraints and additional properties—are published in the machine-readable API catalog under aiBridge.sharedRelayTools . title: AI assistants and documentation search
description: How people and AI tools can find accurate Realot Studio documentation from the documentation URL alone.
headings: Use engine source as the ground truth
content: One URL is enough to start Fetch llms.txt from the documentation root, then query api/search?q=your%20question . The search endpoint returns the closest matching guides and API pages with the correct relative URLs. Pages are directly readable Each guide is static HTML with the full article text, headings, links, tables and code examples already in the page. JavaScript enhances navigation and search; it is not required to retrieve the documentation content. Every guide also has a Markdown twin at the same path with the .md suffix. title: Coordinate system & conventions
description: The signs, units, axes, rotation conventions and reference-resolution rules that prevent common Realot Studio scripting mistakes.
content: Core convention Realot Studio is a 2D screen-style coordinate system: +X is right and +Y is down. Treat Y signs accordingly when writing movement, offsets, camera/UI positioning, and physics examples. Transform axes Value Positive direction Common use x Right Horizontal world movement and placement. y Down Vertical placement; jumping/falling code should use negative/positive signs according to the movement system being used. z Depth layer / pseudo-3D input Affects pseudo-3D rendering only when the camera’s pseudo-3D behavior is enabled. rotation Degrees around Z Used by sprites, lights and directional orientation; 0 points along +X for directional/spot style aiming. scaleX / scaleY 1 = native size Values above 1 enlarge; values below 1 shrink; negative values mirror the axis. UI coordinates Screen-space Text, TextInput, ChatLog and Joystick components use the reference-resolution pixel convention supplied by the Camera/device-fit pipeline. This is why HUD coordinates remain stable when the physical device resolution changes. Angles and vectors Vector-like APIs use ordinary JavaScript objects such as {x, y} . When converting a direction to an angle, remember that the canvas/world Y axis points downward, so visually “up” is negative Y. Timing Concept Meaning time.deltaTime Seconds since the previous script update; multiply speeds expressed per second by deltaTime. wait(seconds,...) Wall-clock game/script timer in seconds. repathInterval Navigation re-plan period in seconds.

title: Debugging
description: Diagnose common Realot Studio runtime and authoring problems.
content: Use the Debug HUD The debug module can show the HUD, FPS and logging. Performance/profiling displays are useful while diagnosing update and rendering behavior. Lifecycle failures If a lifecycle callback throws, the runtime reports the error and isolates it. Look for the callback name and error classification in the runtime output. Physics checklist Confirm the entity has the expected Rigidbody2D body type. Confirm Collider2D shape, layer and mask settings. For one-way platforms, test motion from both sides. Use physics.raycast(...,{debug:true}) to verify what the query actually sees. Navigation checklist Confirm a NavWorld2D exists in the scene. Confirm the queried point is inside walkable bounds. Check NavAgent2D radius/area settings. Use nav.findPath(...,{debug:true}) to visualize the result. Common API mistake Editor code is not game code If code is only found in project/editor/ , it is not automatically a supported game-script API. The public script surface is the documented this.* context and global runtime modules.

title: Live updates
description: How the hosted Realot Studio website and its documentation are updated in place.
headings: The website address stays the same
content: Browser delivery Realot Studio is delivered as a web application. The hosted Hub, editor and runtime are loaded from the site's published files. Users do not need to download a new engine installer whenever the site owner publishes an update. The website address stays the same Publishing a new engine build replaces the files served at the existing deployment URL. The same is true of the documentation: its unversioned topic URLs point to the current published documentation. Browser and PWA caching A normal browser visit retrieves the published site files according to the deployment's cache headers. An installed PWA or a browser with the service worker may continue using cached files while offline. Reconnect and reload to allow the new published files to be fetched. A deployment should publish its files atomically and configure cache headers so the HTML entry points and service worker can update. Project compatibility is separate Although the hosted engine is updated in place, saved project archives may contain engine compatibility metadata. When a project saved by a newer engine is opened in an older build, Realot may show a compatibility warning. That project metadata is not a documentation URL version.

title: Realot Studio reference for AI assistants
description: Practical rules for AI assistants that explain, script, debug and extend Realot Studio projects accurately.
content: What is Realot Studio? Realot Studio is a browser-based 2D game engine with a visual editor, an entity/component runtime, JavaScript gameplay scripts, PixiJS rendering and Rapier2D physics. The Hub and editor run as web applications. The hosted build is updated by publishing web files; users do not install a separate engine executable. Retrieve the relevant reference first Given only the documentation homepage URL, fetch llms.txt from its root, then send the user question to api/search?q=... . Read the closest returned pages; the endpoint supplies their paths, so do not guess URLs. For API questions, also fetch api/index.json and the complete script module member index . The JSON catalog is generated from source facts and is the authoritative list of supported component fields, enum values and API module members. Read the linked guide for behavior, prerequisites and examples. AI Bridge and editor automation When an MCP-connected assistant needs to inspect or edit the open project, use the AI Bridge and MCP guide . It lists the current tools, connection requirements and limits. Do not assume the hosted relay is deployed: it requires a Realot operator to configure it. The MCP tool schemas supplied by the live connection are authoritative for parameters. Gameplay script model Inside a script callback, this refers to the entity that owns the script. Transform shortcuts such as this.x and this.y are always available. Component sub-objects such as this.rigidbody , this.sprite and this.camera require their matching components. this.transform , this.state and this.myTouch are available on every entity. Use the this reference for the full context model. Source and runtime rules Use only documented member names in the module allow-lists; unknown member names raise a typed runtime API error. The member index also flags a known allow-list gap: this.joint.flexibility is listed but has no working script accessor in the supplied source; set it in the Inspector. Check component requirements before suggesting a component-backed API. Use onUpdate(dt) for frame-time behavior and onFixedUpdate(dt) for fixed-step logic. Use entity/world coordinates for Transform, mouse/touch world positions, physics hits and navigation waypoints. Screen coordinates are canvas pixels. Do not reach into editor implementation files from gameplay scripts. Keep editor-only code and runtime code separate. Project scripts execute as page code; imported scripts should be treated as executable content, not as a secure sandbox. Editor settings and components The editor has no single general Settings dialog. Project/backup choices are in File, layer and navigation-area names are in Edit, panel visibility is in Window, and component fields are in the Inspector. The Editor settings guide lists all current menu options and stored performance defaults. The API index links all 25 components and their settings. Export behavior HTML5: downloads a standalone web game package. PWA: adds a manifest and service worker for installation/offline support. Android APK: the user clicks Export, chooses Android APK, and downloads the built APK when the remote service finishes. The current editor allowance is 3 APK exports in a rolling 14-day period. A failed or cancelled job returns its count. The output is debug-signed, not Play Store production-signed. Desktop: shown as coming soon in the supplied Export window. Project files The official portable project file uses the .realot extension. Users can install Realot Hub as a PWA on a supported desktop browser, then double-click a downloaded .realot file to open that project in the editor. Realot can request permission to save changes back to the same file. If PWA file handling is unavailable, users can open the editor and choose File → Load Project .

title: Project format
description: Understand the portable .realot archive and the difference between editable projects and standalone game exports.
content: Current project file Save Project downloads a .realot file. The extension identifies Realot's portable project file, which the editor reads as a complete project package. Archive contents Entry Purpose manifest.json Project name, engine compatibility metadata and save information. scenes/index.json Scene list and active scene information. scenes/*.json Serialized scene entities and component data. assets/sprites.json , frames.json , audio.json Asset catalogues and references to binary asset files. assets/bin/ Binary image/audio data referenced by the asset catalogues. scripts.json User-authored JavaScript source. prefabs.json Saved prefab definitions. layers.json , navAreas.json , tags.json Project-wide layer, navigation-area and tag names. Open a project Use the editor's File → Load Project command to open a saved .realot project. On a desktop browser that supports PWA file handling, you can also install Realot Hub and double-click a downloaded .realot file to open it in the editor. Project archive versus game export A .realot archive is an editable project that can be loaded back into the editor. An HTML5/PWA export is a separate standalone game package with index.html at its root, containing the runtime and files needed to run the game. The Android build service consumes the standalone game export, not the editable project file. Compatibility metadata The project manifest includes engine compatibility metadata. The loader compares it with the engine build and can warn when a project was saved by a newer engine. This metadata belongs to the project format; it is not a documentation version or a user-facing engine download version.

title: Engine conventions (RULES.txt)
description: The architectural rules that govern how Realot Studio’s own codebase is organized.
headings: 1. The core rule: runtime never depends on editor
2. One feature = new file(s), not a growing old file
5. Scene data flows through the runtime’s public API only
content: Scope This is the engine’s own internal contract for where code goes and how the three top-level folders relate. It applies to people extending Realot Studio itself; if you’re only writing game scripts, you don’t need it — see Scripting quickstart instead. 1. The core rule: runtime never depends on editor runtime/ is the actual game engine. editor/ is the Unity-style level editor UI, a development tool only. target/ is the standalone game shell, importing only from runtime/ . No file under runtime/ may ever import, reference, or depend on anything under editor/ — not for debugging, not temporarily, not ever. You must be able to delete the editor/ folder entirely and the game ( standalone runtime play entry point ) keeps working with zero changes. editor/ may import from runtime/ — that direction is allowed and expected, since the editor is built on top of the engine. 2. One feature = new file(s), not a growing old file Adding a new component, system, editor panel, scripting API, or asset type creates a new file in the appropriate subfolder. Unrelated functionality is never appended into an existing file just because it’s nearby or already open. If a feature doesn’t fit any existing subfolder, a new subfolder is created (matching the existing lowercase, pluralized naming style) rather than dumping it into an unrelated folder. Adding… Goes in… A new gameplay component runtime/components/YourComponent.js A new gameplay/rendering/physics system runtime/systems/YourSystem.js A new editor panel editor/panels/YourPanel.js A new asset type runtime/assets/YourManager.js A new scripting capability A method/property on the relevant file in runtime/scripting/components/, or a new file there 3. Components stay plain data Files under runtime/components/ hold only plain serializable data (numbers, strings, booleans). No PixiJS objects, no DOM references, no behavior/update logic — behavior belongs in runtime/systems/ . This is what keeps SceneSerializer.js able to save and load any component generically. 4. Rendering is centralized runtime/systems/RenderSystem.js is the only place that creates or updates PixiJS display objects from entity data. Both the editor’s viewport and the standalone target use it, so visuals never drift between edit mode and play mode. Editor-only chrome (grid lines, selection gizmos) may be drawn in its own separate layer on top of the runtime’s render output — that chrome must never be visible in /target . 5. Scene data flows through the runtime’s public API only The editor never invents its own scene format or its own copy of scene state. The single source of truth is the live World instance, and the single way to read/write its persisted form is runtime/scene/SceneSerializer.js . New scene-level functionality (undo, multi-scene, prefabs) extends the runtime’s scene/ folder, not the editor’s state/ folder. One API per capability (scripting) this.x , this.y , this.position , this.rotation , this.translate() , and this.visible are flat shortcuts because Transform has only one shape. Everything else — velocity, physics forces, sprite properties, animation, camera, audio, movement-type tunables — is reached only through its sub-object ( this.rigidbody.* , this.sprite.* , this.controller.* , etc). There is deliberately no flat-shortcut duplicate of any of these, because RigidbodyAPI exposes a different shape per body type and ControllerAPI exposes a different shape per controller type — a second flat copy would either duplicate that per-type logic or drift out of sync with it. Source note These rules come from the engine repository’s RULES.txt . That file is not included in the client distribution ( project/ contains editor/ , player/ , runtime/ and vendor/ only), so it is documented here rather than linked.

There is deliberately no flat-shortcut duplicate of any of these, because RigidbodyAPI exposes a different shape per body type and ControllerAPI exposes a different shape per controller type — a second flat copy would either duplicate that per-type logic or drift out of sync with it. Source note These rules come from the engine repository’s RULES.txt . That file is not included in the client distribution ( project/ contains editor/ , player/ , runtime/ and vendor/ only), so it is documented here rather than linked.

title: Scene JSON
description: Reference the Realot Studio scene serialization format.
content: Top-level shape json { "sceneName" : "Level1" , "hierarchyFolders" : [], "entities" : [] } Entity shape json { "id" : "e12" , "name" : "Target" , "tag" : "Target" , "active" : true , "folderId" : null , "prefabId" : null , "prefabOverrides" : {}, "components" : { "Transform" : { "x" : 0 , "y" : 0 , "z" : 0 , "rotation" : 0 , "scaleX" : 1 , "scaleY" : 1 } } } Component registry SceneSerializer recognizes the runtime component types: Transform, Camera, SpriteRenderer, ShapeRenderer, StrokePath, TextRenderer, SpeechBubble, ChatLog, TextInput, Joystick, Rigidbody2D, Collider2D, Joint2D, Light, ShadowCaster, CharacterController, LightingSettings, SpriteAnimation, AudioSource, AudioListener, Tileset, Tilemap, NavWorld2D, NavAgent2D and Script. Authoring rules Scene files are plain JSON and can be authored by the editor, generated by tools or hand-written. The serializer deep-copies folder/prefab override data so saved snapshots do not alias live state. Default camera A fresh/default scene uses a Main Camera entity with tag MainCamera , active state enabled, Transform at 0,0 and a main Camera flag.

title: Security and play origin
description: Understand the script trust boundary and why shared projects should run on a separate origin.
headings: Use a separate play origin for shared projects
content: Game scripts are not a security sandbox Project scripts execute as ordinary JavaScript in the game page. Treat scripts inside imported projects as code from another person, not as inert project data. Script execution Realot shadows selected browser globals inside its script environment as a guardrail against accidental access. This is not a hardened security boundary: scripts are compiled and run as page code. Do not open a project containing scripts unless you trust its source. Use a separate play origin for shared projects For a deployment where people can open projects from others, configure the editor to launch Play on a separate hostname that serves the same Realot files. In project/editor/index.html , set the realot-play-origin meta tag to that HTTPS origin: html < meta name = "realot-play-origin" content = "https://play.example.com" /> The editor sends the scene to the play page using postMessage . Because the two hostnames are different origins, browser same-origin policy keeps the play page's localStorage, IndexedDB and DOM separate from the editor's. Leave the meta content empty and Play uses the same origin; that is less isolated and is not recommended for untrusted projects. Offline behavior If the configured play origin cannot be reached, such as while offline, the editor can fall back to same-origin Play and logs a warning. Data saved by the game on the play origin is separate from the editor origin's storage. Other protections Messages are accepted only from the corresponding editor/play window and expected origin. Console output and project-controlled names are escaped before display in the editor UI. Loading a project containing scripts asks for confirmation first. Exported games run on the origin where the developer hosts them; they are separate from the editor's Play-origin setting. APK build credentials The APK service URL is public configuration. Permanent service credentials must not be placed in the static editor source because all shipped JavaScript can be inspected by visitors. The editor's intended managed flow requests a short-lived token from the service and renews it when needed. The service must still enforce appropriate quotas and access controls; a public token-issuance endpoint alone does not identify an approved user.

title: Source map & verification
description: A source-grounded map of where Realot Studio’s public behavior and editor controls are actually implemented.
headings: Important source files for documentation truth
content: Verified source This documentation pass was checked against the supplied Realot Studio engine source, including runtime components, scripting API modules, editor panels/state, navigation, physics, scene serialization, and export code. Engine architecture map Area Primary source locations Purpose Public runtime entry project/runtime/index.js Wires World + systems + scripting and exposes createGame(). Components project/runtime/components/ Serializable component data used by scene entities. Systems project/runtime/systems/ Runtime behavior such as physics, rendering, animation, lighting, audio, navigation and scripting. Scripting project/runtime/scripting/ User-facing script surface, EntityContext and option metadata. Physics project/runtime/physics/ Rapier-backed collider/body/joint queries and contact behavior. Navigation project/runtime/pathfinding/ A* grid bake, dynamic bake, area masks/costs and navigation support. Editor UI project/editor/panels/ Toolbar, Hierarchy, Inspector, Project/Console, animation, tileset, export and settings windows. Editor state/events project/editor/state/ Persistence, dirty state, layer/area registries and DOM event handling. Scene serialization project/runtime/scene/SceneSerializer.js Serialized scene/entity component format. title: Tuning guide
description: Practical “increase/decrease this” rules for movement, physics, navigation, lighting, UI and path authoring.
content: How to tune movement Goal Raise Lower More responsive character movement acceleration, airControl acceleration, airControl Longer/faster jump jumpForce, maxJumps if desired gravityScale / jumpForce More stable vehicle turn/brake smoothing, recovery settings overly aggressive steering values Faster NavAgent speed, acceleration stoppingDistance if you want it closer before stopping How to tune physics Goal Typical setting Direction Make dynamic body fall faster Rigidbody2D.gravityScale Increase above 1. Make body coast longer linearDamping Decrease toward 0. Make body stop rotating sooner angularDamping Increase. Make contact bouncier Collider2D.restitution Increase. Reduce sliding Collider2D.friction Increase. Make a platform one-way Collider2D.isOneWayPlatform Enable; contact filtering then only allows landing from the supported side. How to tune navigation Setting Increase means Decrease means NavWorld2D.cellSize coarser/faster grid, less geometric detail finer grid, narrower detail but more work NavAgent2D.radius larger clearance requirement smaller agent clearance NavAgent2D.repathInterval less frequent replanning more responsive replanning NavWorld2D.areaCosts slot more expensive path cost through that area closer to the cheapest route How to tune lighting Setting Increase means Decrease means Light.intensity brighter/stronger contribution dimmer Light.radius larger influence region tighter/localized light ShadowCaster.length longer shadow reach shorter/contact shadow ShadowCaster.softness softer/wider penumbra crisper edge LightingSettings.raymarchSteps more samples/detail, more GPU work less GPU work, potentially less detail LightingSettings.ambientDarkness darker unlit regions brighter ambient base Rule for numeric documentation Realot Studio documentation should state not only what a field is, but what increasing and decreasing it does, its units, default, and whether the value is clamped/validated. The API catalog in api-options.json follows this model for option objects.

title: Script API cookbook
description: Concrete Realot Studio script examples with setup, placement, required components, options, expected behavior, and common mistakes.
headings: 1. Find an entity and move toward it
4. Send an event without hard-coding the receiver's logic
6. Delay work without hand-written countdown variables
8. Ask the navigation system for a path
10. Use named navigation areas instead of raw bitmasks
14. Trigger a scene change on overlap
15. Build your own tiny diagnostic HUD
content: How to use the cookbook Every example assumes a Script component exists on the entity that owns the code. In the editor, select the entity in the left Hierarchy, then use the right Inspector to open its Script component. Paste the example into the script's lifecycle function or adapt it to your existing script. Read API reference + recipe together The API reference tells you what a function/property means. The recipes show when to call it, what object should own the script, and what other setup the feature needs. 1. Find an entity and move toward it Setup Create an entity named Target . Put this script on the enemy. Code js function onUpdate ( dt ) { var target = findFirst ( "Target" ); if ( ! target ) return ; this . navMoveToward ( target . x , target . y , 140 ); } findFirst(name) returns one matching entity or null . navMoveToward() supplies the navigation movement behavior. 2. Spawn a runtime clone Author a source entity in the scene first, for example an entity named Bullet . The script below can live on a target, weapon, or spawner. js var bullet = spawn ( "Bullet" , { x : this . x + 24 , y : this . y , name : "Bullet_Instance" }); if ( bullet ) { bullet . velocityX = 500 ; } Why the source entity matters spawn() clones an existing authored entity. It is not a constructor that invents a new component set from scratch. 3. Raycast toward an entity Put this on the entity performing the vision/sensor check. js function onUpdate ( dt ) { var target = findFirst ( "Target" ); if ( ! target ) return ; var hit = physics . raycast ( this . x , this . y , target . x , target . y , { layerMask : 1 << 0 , exclude : [ this ], debug : true }); this . hasLineOfSight = ! hit || hit . entity === target ; } The result is either a hit object containing entity , point , normal , and distance , or a falsy result when nothing is hit. 4. Send an event without hard-coding the receiver's logic js // Sender var enemy = findFirst ( "Enemy" ); if ( enemy ) sendMessage ( enemy , "takeDamage" , { amount : 25 }); // Receiver function onMessage ( message , sender , data ) { if ( message === "takeDamage" ) { this . hp -= data . amount ; } } Use an EntityContext when you need exactly one receiver. Use a tag string when you intentionally want a group to receive the same message. 5. Keyboard movement with frame-independent speed js function onUpdate ( dt ) { var dx = 0 ; var dy = 0 ; if ( input . keyDown ( "ArrowLeft" )) dx -= 1 ; if ( input . keyDown ( "ArrowRight" )) dx += 1 ; if ( input . keyDown ( "ArrowUp" )) dy -= 1 ; if ( input . keyDown ( "ArrowDown" )) dy += 1 ; var length = Math . hypot ( dx , dy ); if ( length > 0 ) { dx /= length ; dy /= length ; this . x += dx * 220 * dt ; this . y += dy * 220 * dt ; } } This is useful for simple non-physics entities. Use Rigidbody2D/CharacterController APIs when movement is supposed to participate in physics/controller resolution. 6. Delay work without hand-written countdown variables js function onStart () { this . wait ( 1.5 , function () { this . sprite . opacity = 0.4 ; }); this . repeat ( 2 , function () { debug . log ( "heartbeat" ); }); } Entity-owned timers are automatically cancelled when the scheduling entity is destroyed or the scene changes. 7. Persistent save data js function onStart () { this . hp = save . get ( "targetHp" ) ?? 100 ; } function onCheckpointReached () { save . set ( "targetHp" , this . hp ); save . set ( "checkpoint" , { x : this . x , y : this . y }); } async function onGameComplete () { save . set ( "completed" , true ); await save . flushNow (); scene . load ( "Credits" ); } Important save.set() updates the in-memory save immediately. Use await save.flushNow() when the next action must wait for durable storage before continuing. 8. Ask the navigation system for a path js var path = nav . findPath ( this . x , this . y , goalX , goalY , { radius : this . navAgent . radius , area : nav . areaMask ( "Ground" , "Road" ), areaCosts : nav . areaCosts ({ Road : 1 , Mud : 4 }), debug : true }); if ( path ) { debug . log ( "Waypoints: " + path . length ); } This example demonstrates four separate concepts: agent clearance, hard area permission, soft area preference, and debug visualization. 9. Change a NavAgent2D at runtime Select the moving entity and add Nav Agent 2D in Inspector → Add Component → Nav Agent 2D . The exposed script properties are read/write. js this . navAgent . speed = 180 ; this . navAgent . radius = 12 ; this . navAgent . avoidanceEnabled = true ; this . navAgent . repathInterval = 0.2 ; // Read-only current route state: var path = this . navAgent . currentPath ; var index = this . navAgent . currentPathIndex ; Read-only fields currentPath and currentPathIndex are managed by navMoveToward() . Do not assign to them; call this.navMoveToward(newX,newY,...) to change the destination. 10. Use named navigation areas instead of raw bitmasks First name the slots in Edit → Nav Areas… . For example: Ground , Road , Mud , Water . js var roadOnly = nav . areaMask ( "Road" ); var mixed = nav . areaMask ( "Road" , "Ground" ); var waterSlot = nav . areaIndex ( "Water" ); This keeps scripts readable and means you do not have to remember which slot number was assigned to each named area. 11. Camera follow js function onUpdate ( dt ) { var target = findFirst ( "Target" ); if ( target ) { this . camera . follow ( target , { smoothing : 0.1 }); } } Put the script on the entity that has the Camera component. The engine template also demonstrates this pattern. 12. Switch animations from gameplay state js function onUpdate ( dt ) { if ( ! this . rigidbody ) return ; if ( ! this . rigidbody . grounded ) { if ( this . rigidbody . velocityY > 0 ) this . animator . play ( "fall" ); else this . animator . play ( "Jump" ); } else if ( Math . abs ( this . rigidbody . velocityX ) > 5 ) { this . animator . play ( "Run" ); } else { this . animator . play ( "Idle" ); } } 13. Touch / joystick control For a Joystick component, select an entity, then use Inspector → Add Component → Joystick . The script can read normalized values: js function onUpdate ( dt ) { if ( ! this . joystick || ! this . joystick . active ) return ; this . controller . simulateMove ( this . joystick . x , this . joystick . y ); } x and y are normalized joystick axes; magnitude tells you how far the thumb is displaced. 14. Trigger a scene change on overlap Give the portal entity a Collider2D and enable its Is Trigger checkbox in the right Inspector. js function onTriggerEnter ( other ) { if ( other . name === "Target" ) { scene . load ( "Level2" ); } } Trigger callbacks depend on Collider2D overlap. A trigger does not behave like a solid blocking collider. 15. Build your own tiny diagnostic HUD js function onUpdate ( dt ) { debug . log ( "pos=" + Math . round ( this . x ) + "," + Math . round ( this . y ) + " speed=" + Math . round ( this . navAgent ? this . navAgent . speed : 0 ) ); } Use this while developing, then remove or gate noisy logging before a final release. Patterns that scale well Need Prefer Avoid Exact entity findById() or a known EntityContext Assuming a shared name is unique when it is not. Group communication Tag + sendMessage() Duplicating the same lookup in every receiver. Persistent data save.* Using global.* for data that must survive reload. Pathfinding One NavWorld2D + NavAgent2D per mover Creating a navigation world per NPC. Physics movement Rigidbody2D / CharacterController APIs Directly changing x/y when you need collision resolution. Frame-independent custom movement Multiply speed by dt Using a raw pixels-per-frame constant. Where to go next Complete Navigation Full editor-to-runtime navigation setup, areas, costs, vehicles and debugging. Option schemas Exact opts objects, defaults, types and override rules. Component reference Every component and its editor/runtime contract.

Switch animations from gameplay state js function onUpdate ( dt ) { if ( ! this . rigidbody ) return ; if ( ! this . rigidbody . grounded ) { if ( this . rigidbody . velocityY > 0 ) this . animator . play ( "fall" ); else this . animator . play ( "Jump" ); } else if ( Math . abs ( this . rigidbody . velocityX ) > 5 ) { this . animator . play ( "Run" ); } else { this . animator . play ( "Idle" ); } } 13. Touch / joystick control For a Joystick component, select an entity, then use Inspector → Add Component → Joystick . The script can read normalized values: js function onUpdate ( dt ) { if ( ! this . joystick || ! this . joystick . active ) return ; this . controller . simulateMove ( this . joystick . x , this . joystick . y ); } x and y are normalized joystick axes; magnitude tells you how far the thumb is displaced. 14. Trigger a scene change on overlap Give the portal entity a Collider2D and enable its Is Trigger checkbox in the right Inspector. js function onTriggerEnter ( other ) { if ( other . name === "Target" ) { scene . load ( "Level2" ); } } Trigger callbacks depend on Collider2D overlap. A trigger does not behave like a solid blocking collider. 15. Build your own tiny diagnostic HUD js function onUpdate ( dt ) { debug . log ( "pos=" + Math . round ( this . x ) + "," + Math . round ( this . y ) + " speed=" + Math . round ( this . navAgent ? this . navAgent . speed : 0 ) ); } Use this while developing, then remove or gate noisy logging before a final release. Patterns that scale well Need Prefer Avoid Exact entity findById() or a known EntityContext Assuming a shared name is unique when it is not. Group communication Tag + sendMessage() Duplicating the same lookup in every receiver. Persistent data save.* Using global.* for data that must survive reload. Pathfinding One NavWorld2D + NavAgent2D per mover Creating a navigation world per NPC. Physics movement Rigidbody2D / CharacterController APIs Directly changing x/y when you need collision resolution. Frame-independent custom movement Multiply speed by dt Using a raw pixels-per-frame constant. title: Collisions & triggers
description: onCollisionEnter/Stay/Exit, onTriggerEnter/Exit, the other parameter, and physics layers from script.
content: Requirements Collision and trigger callbacks need a Collider2D on the entity receiving the callback (a Rigidbody2D is not strictly required — a collider with no rigidbody is treated as static, matching how Unity handles a collider-only object). The other parameter other in every collision/trigger callback is an EntityContext — the exact same shape as this . You can read other.x , other.name , call other.hasComponent(...) , or even other.destroy() . Enter vs. Stay vs. Exit js function onCollisionEnter ( other ) { if ( other . name === "Ground" ) this . isGrounded = true ; } function onCollisionExit ( other ) { if ( other . name === "Ground" ) this . isGrounded = false ; } onCollisionStay(other) fires every physics step the collider remains touching — from the step after Enter, up to (not including) the step Exit fires. Use Stay sparingly for continuous effects (e.g. damage-over-time while standing in a hazard); use Enter/Exit for one-shot state changes. Triggers A collider with isTrigger: true detects overlap without physically blocking movement, and fires onTriggerEnter / onTriggerExit instead of the collision events: js function onTriggerEnter ( other ) { if ( other . hasComponent ( "Rigidbody2D" )) { scene . load ( "Level2" ); } } Physics layers Collider2D’s layer / mask fields (16 named layers, same slot-based model as Unity) control which pairs of colliders physically interact and receive callbacks at all. Two colliders only interact if each one’s membership layer is included in the other’s mask — see Collider2D for the full bitmask reference and physics.layer(...) for building a mask from script.

title: Entity context
description: Reference the `this` object and entity-aware shortcuts available in Realot Studio scripts.
content: Core members Member Meaning x, y World position; writes to physics position targets when a non-static Rigidbody2D exists. position Read/assign {x,y}. rotation Degrees. scaleX, scaleY Scale. translate(dx,dy) Move by a delta. distanceTo(x,y) Distance to a world point. name Read-only entity name. tag Read/write tag. id Stable unique ID. visible Show/hide entity. enabled Enable/disable the current script. destroy() Queue entity destruction. destroyed Read-only destruction state. isClone True for runtime-spawned clones. js function onUpdate () { this . translate ( 0 , - 50 * time . deltaTime ); // move up var target = findFirst ( "Target" ); if ( target && this . distanceTo ( target . x , target . y ) < 40 ) { this . destroy (); } } Component modules Depending on attached components, this exposes modules including transform , sprite , shape , text , speechBubble , chat , textInput , joystick , rigidbody , controller , animator , camera , audio , ear , collider , joint , navAgent , light , shadowCaster and strokePath . js function onUpdate () { if ( this . hasComponent ( "Rigidbody2D" )) { this . rigidbody . addForce ( 0 , - 500 ); } this . sprite . opacity = this . isPointerOver ? 1 : 0.6 ; } Timers belong to entities Both wait() and repeat() are associated with the scheduling entity. When the entity is destroyed or a scene restarts/switches, its timers are automatically cancelled. js function onStart () { this . wait ( 1.5 , function () { this . sprite . opacity = 1 ; // this is still the entity that scheduled the timer }); } Pointer helpers Collider requirement isPointerOver , isClicked , isTouchOver , isTapped and myTouch require Collider2D because hit testing uses the real collider shape.

title: Entity shortcuts (this.x, this.transform)
description: What this is inside a script, which properties are flat shortcuts, and which require a specific component.
content: Flat shortcuts (always available) Inside any lifecycle function, this is an EntityContext bound to the entity the script is attached to. A small set of properties are flat shortcuts directly onto the entity’s Transform, because Transform has only one shape. Everything else lives behind a sub-object gated by a specific component — see the full this reference for every sub-object. Shortcut Meaning this.x / this.y Read/write live position. Writing immediately moves the entity, and correctly teleports the physics body too on a Dynamic or Kinematic Rigidbody2D rather than being silently overwritten by the next physics step. this.position {x, y}; assigning moves the entity. this.translate(dx, dy) Move by a delta this call. this.rotation, this.scaleX, this.scaleY Degrees and scale factors, matching the Inspector’s Transform fields. this.visible, this.enabled Show/hide and enable/disable the entity. js function onUpdate () { this . rotation += 90 * time . deltaTime ; // spin this . translate ( 0 , - 1 ); // drift upward one unit per frame if ( this . y < - 50 ) this . visible = false ; } Identity & lifecycle helpers Helper Meaning this.destroy() Queues the entity for removal (deferred, not instant). this.destroyed becomes true immediately even though removal has not happened yet. this.hasComponent(key) True if the entity currently has the named component. "Transform" always returns true. Works on any EntityContext, including one from find() or a collision callback’s other. this.name, this.tag, this.id Read-only name; read/write tag; stable unique ID. this.isClone True inside onClone()/onStart() for a runtime-spawned clone. js function onUpdate () { if ( this . hp <= 0 && ! this . destroyed ) { this . destroy (); } } function onStart () { if ( this . isClone ) this . tag = "spawned" ; // mark runtime clones differently }

title: Errors & debugging
description: How script errors are classified and reported, and the on-screen debug HUD.
content: How errors are reported A thrown error inside one lifecycle call is caught right there and reported to the editor Console — it does not disable the whole script (except onStart , which only ever runs once). Identical errors repeating every frame are throttled: reported immediately once, then suppressed and periodically summarized with a repeat count, so a bug in onUpdate doesn’t spam the console 60 times a second. Error kinds Errors thrown by the scripting API are tagged with a machine-readable kind so the Console can show a specific, actionable message instead of a generic "X is not a function": Kind Meaning Example missing-component Accessed this.rigidbody/.sprite/etc. but the entity does not have that component at all. this.sprite.opacity on an entity with no Sprite Renderer unsupported-body-type Called a member that does not apply to this entity’s current body/controller type. this.rigidbody.addForce() on a Kinematic or Static body unknown-api A property or method that does not exist at all — almost always a typo. this.rigidbody.addFrce() script-error Anything without a kind — a plain script bug (null dereference, bad logic, etc). — Every unknown-api error also lists the valid member names for that sub-object, so a typo is a one-line fix rather than a trip back to this documentation. The on-screen debug HUD js debug . show (); // turn the HUD on (visible in the Play window, not the editor console) debug . showFps ( false ); // keep the HUD on but hide just the FPS line debug . log ( "Target HP" , this . hp ); debug . clear ( "Target HP" ); debug . clearAll ();

title: Finding & spawning entities
description: The find/findAll/findWithTag family, plus spawn() for runtime-instantiated clones.
content: Finding entities API Returns findFirst(name) First entity with this exact name, or null. findAll(name) Every entity with this name, as an array. findFirstWithTag(tag) / findAllWithTag(tag) Same pair, keyed by tag instead of name. findById(id) Never ambiguous — use the id from an earlier spawn() or find() call. findInRadius(x, y, radius, opts) Entities within radius world units of a point, nearest first. entity.distanceTo(x, y) Instance method on any EntityContext: distance from that entity to a point. Spawning spawn(nameOrTag, opts) spawns a runtime clone of an existing entity. Looks the source up by name by default: js spawn ( "Bullet" ); spawn ( "Bullet" , { x : this . x , y : this . y }); spawn ( "Enemy" , { byTag : true , x : 200 , y : 100 }); // look up by tag, clone the first match Optionally rename the clone with opts.name . Returns an EntityContext for the new entity (same shape as this ), or null if no source entity matches. The clone’s own onClone() then onStart() fire automatically on the next frame, with this.isClone === true inside them. Also available as an instance method, this.spawn(nameOrTagOrEntity, opts) — pass an EntityContext directly (e.g. this.spawn(this) ) to clone that exact entity with zero name/tag ambiguity.

title: Global scripting API
description: Reference for every built-in global function and service object available inside Realot Studio scripts.
content: Entity lookup Function Returns / behavior findFirst(name) First entity with this name, or null . findAll(name) All entities with this name. findFirstWithTag(tag) First entity with this tag, or null . findAllWithTag(tag) All entities with this tag. findWithTag(tag) Alias for findAllWithTag(tag) . findById(id) Entity with this exact stable ID, or null . findInRadius(x, y, radius, opts?) Nearby entities, nearest first. Optional filters can narrow the search. Scene ( scene ) scene contains the same entity-lookup functions above, plus load(sceneName) , restart() , pause() , resume() , the read-only properties current and isPaused , and scene-wide lighting . scene.pause() freezes gameplay simulation while leaving the editor/Play window responsive; call scene.resume() to continue. Physics ( physics ) physics.raycast(x1, y1, x2, y2, opts?) casts a ray against Rapier collider shapes and returns the closest hit or null . A hit contains the entity, world point, surface normal (when available) and distance. Pass { exclude: [this] } to skip an entity, { debug: true } to draw the ray for one frame, or { layerMask: physics.layer(0, 2) } to filter by layer bits. physics.layer(...indices) creates the bitmask for slots 0–15. js function onUpdate () { var hit = physics . raycast ( this . x , this . y , this . x + 200 , this . y , { exclude : [ this ], debug : true }); if ( hit ) debug . log ( "Ray hit" , hit . entity . name ); } Navigation ( nav ) Member Purpose findPath(x1, y1, x2, y2, opts?) Returns world-space waypoints or null when no route is available. isWalkable(x, y) Tests whether a world point falls on a walkable navigation cell. bake() Rebuilds the scene NavWorld2D from current colliders; returns walkable/blocked counts or null . areaIndex(name) Resolves an area name to a slot index, or -1 . areaMask(...names) Builds a bitmask from named areas. areaCosts(costsByName) Builds a 16-entry cost array from area names and positive costs. For moving entities every frame, use this.navMoveToward() or (for a Car controller) this.navDriveToward() . See Pathfinding . Keyboard ( input ) input.keyDown(key) is true while a key is held. input.keyPressed(key) is true only on the frame it is first pressed. Both accept "Any" to test whether any key is held or was pressed that frame. Use the Input guide for key naming and patterns. Mouse and pointer ( mouse ) mouse.x and mouse.y are world coordinates. screenX and screenY are canvas pixels. over reports whether the pointer is over the game canvas. down(button?) , pressed(button?) and released(button?) read mouse buttons (0 left, 1 middle, 2 right; omitted means left). isOver(entityOrName, opts?) tests hover and clickedOn(entityOrName, opts?, button?) tests a click on a specific entity. Touch ( touch ) touch is a live array of active touches. Each touch exposes id , world-space x/y , canvas-pixel screenX/screenY , start coordinates, displacement ( dx/dy ), distance , and one-frame justStarted/justEnded flags. The array also exposes count , first , anyJustStarted and anyJustEnded . Gesture helpers are swipe.active/direction/dx/dy/distance and pinch.active/scale/delta/distance . touch.isOver(entityOrName, opts?) checks a finger over an entity; touch.tappedOn(entityOrName, opts?) detects the initial tap. See Input guide . Time ( time ) time.deltaTime is scaled frame time, time.unscaledDeltaTime is frame time before time scaling, time.elapsed is elapsed game time, and time.scale controls game speed. A scale of 0 pauses time-driven simulation; 1 is normal speed. See Time scale & game speed . Random and math helpers random.int(min, max) returns an inclusive random integer. random.float(min, max) returns a random float in the half-open range [min, max). mathx provides lerp , smoothstep , clamp , moveToward , remap and approximately . A bare smoothstep(a, b, value) global is also available. Native JavaScript Math is available as well. Shared in-memory state ( global ) global is a shared key/value object visible to all scripts in the current running game. Read and write named properties directly, for example global.score = 10 . It is memory-only; it does not survive reloading the game page. Use save for persistent data. Persistent save data ( save ) save stores JSON-safe values in IndexedDB, separated into named save slots. Its full 13-member API is listed in SaveAPI . Common calls are get , set , has , delete , keys and clear . Use await save.load("slot2") to change slots, await save.listSlots() to list them, await save.deleteSlot("slot2") to remove a slot, and await save.flushNow() to wait for pending writes. See Persistence . Debug HUD ( debug ) debug.show() enables the gameplay HUD and system timing display in the Play window; debug.show(false) turns it off. debug.showFps(false) hides only its FPS line. debug.log(label, value) adds or updates a custom line; debug.clear(label) removes one line; debug.clearAll() removes all custom lines. This is separate from the editor Console. Object pools ( pool ) pool.create(name, options) creates a named pool using a source prefab, scene entity or EntityContext. pool.find(name) retrieves a named pool, pool.get(name, x, y) gets an active object, and pool.release(entity) returns it for reuse. A pooled entity can call this.releaseToPool(delay?) . Pooled scripts can use onEnable and onDisable for work that should run each time an object is borrowed or returned. Spawn, timers, messages and tweens Function Behavior spawn(nameOrTag, opts?) Clones an entity found by name, or by tag when opts.byTag is true. Returns an EntityContext or null . wait(seconds, callback) Runs once after game time passes; returns a timer ID. repeat(seconds, callback) Runs repeatedly at the interval; returns a timer ID. cancelWait(id) / cancelRepeat(id) Cancel the matching timer. Entity-owned timers also stop when their owner is destroyed or the scene changes. sendMessage(tagOrEntity, message, data?) Sends to all scripts matching a tag, or one exact entity context. broadcastMessage(message, data?) Sends to every script in the current scene. tween(target, properties, duration, easing?, onComplete?) Animates numeric properties over game time; returns an ID. cancelTween(id) Cancels a running tween. Read Timers, state & messaging , Finding and spawning and Tween API for complete examples and option details. The script module index contains all 24 component/global API module allow-lists.

Both accept "Any" to test whether any key is held or was pressed that frame. Use the Input guide for key naming and patterns. Mouse and pointer ( mouse ) mouse.x and mouse.y are world coordinates. screenX and screenY are canvas pixels. over reports whether the pointer is over the game canvas. down(button?) , pressed(button?) and released(button?) read mouse buttons (0 left, 1 middle, 2 right; omitted means left). isOver(entityOrName, opts?) tests hover and clickedOn(entityOrName, opts?, button?) tests a click on a specific entity. Touch ( touch ) touch is a live array of active touches. Each touch exposes id , world-space x/y , canvas-pixel screenX/screenY , start coordinates, displacement ( dx/dy ), distance , and one-frame justStarted/justEnded flags. The array also exposes count , first , anyJustStarted and anyJustEnded . Gesture helpers are swipe.active/direction/dx/dy/distance and pinch.active/scale/delta/distance . touch.isOver(entityOrName, opts?) checks a finger over an entity; touch.tappedOn(entityOrName, opts?) detects the initial tap. See Input guide . Time ( time ) time.deltaTime is scaled frame time, time.unscaledDeltaTime is frame time before time scaling, time.elapsed is elapsed game time, and time.scale controls game speed. A scale of 0 pauses time-driven simulation; 1 is normal speed. See Time scale & game speed . Random and math helpers random.int(min, max) returns an inclusive random integer. random.float(min, max) returns a random float in the half-open range [min, max). mathx provides lerp , smoothstep , clamp , moveToward , remap and approximately . A bare smoothstep(a, b, value) global is also available. Native JavaScript Math is available as well. Shared in-memory state ( global ) global is a shared key/value object visible to all scripts in the current running game. Read and write named properties directly, for example global.score = 10 . It is memory-only; it does not survive reloading the game page. Use save for persistent data. Persistent save data ( save ) save stores JSON-safe values in IndexedDB, separated into named save slots. Its full 13-member API is listed in SaveAPI . Common calls are get , set , has , delete , keys and clear . Use await save.load("slot2") to change slots, await save.listSlots() to list them, await save.deleteSlot("slot2") to remove a slot, and await save.flushNow() to wait for pending writes. See Persistence . Debug HUD ( debug ) debug.show() enables the gameplay HUD and system timing display in the Play window; debug.show(false) turns it off. debug.showFps(false) hides only its FPS line. debug.log(label, value) adds or updates a custom line; debug.clear(label) removes one line; debug.clearAll() removes all custom lines. This is separate from the editor Console. Object pools ( pool ) pool.create(name, options) creates a named pool using a source prefab, scene entity or EntityContext. pool.find(name) retrieves a named pool, pool.get(name, x, y) gets an active object, and pool.release(entity) returns it for reuse. A pooled entity can call this.releaseToPool(delay?) . Pooled scripts can use onEnable and onDisable for work that should run each time an object is borrowed or returned. Spawn, timers, messages and tweens Function Behavior spawn(nameOrTag, opts?) Clones an entity found by name, or by tag when opts.byTag is true. Returns an EntityContext or null . wait(seconds, callback) Runs once after game time passes; returns a timer ID. repeat(seconds, callback) Runs repeatedly at the interval; returns a timer ID. cancelWait(id) / cancelRepeat(id) Cancel the matching timer. Entity-owned timers also stop when their owner is destroyed or the scene changes. sendMessage(tagOrEntity, message, data?) Sends to all scripts matching a tag, or one exact entity context. broadcastMessage(message, data?) Sends to every script in the current scene. tween(target, properties, duration, easing?, onComplete?) Animates numeric properties over game time; returns an ID. cancelTween(id) Cancels a running tween. Read Timers, state & messaging , Finding and spawning and Tween API for complete examples and option details. The script module index contains all 24 component/global API module allow-lists.

title: Input
description: Keyboard, mouse, touch, gestures and virtual joystick input in Realot Studio.
content: Keyboard input.keyDown(code) is true while a key is held. input.keyPressed(code) is a one-frame pulse. Browser-style codes include ArrowLeft , ArrowRight , KeyA , Space and the special code Any . js function onUpdate () { var speed = 200 * time . deltaTime ; if ( input . keyDown ( "ArrowRight" ) || input . keyDown ( "KeyD" )) this . x += speed ; if ( input . keyDown ( "ArrowLeft" ) || input . keyDown ( "KeyA" )) this . x -= speed ; if ( input . keyPressed ( "Space" )) { this . controller . simulateJump (); // one-frame pulse — fires once per press, not every frame held } } Mouse API Semantics mouse.x / mouse.y World-space cursor position. mouse.screenX / mouse.screenY Raw canvas-pixel cursor position. mouse.down(button) Held button; 0 left, 1 middle, 2 right. mouse.pressed(button) Pressed this frame. mouse.released(button) Released this frame. mouse.isOver(target) Shape-accurate entity hit test. mouse.clickedOn(target) Hit test + pressed pulse. js function onUpdate () { if ( mouse . clickedOn ( this . name )) { this . destroy (); // click this entity to pop it } // or, from inside the entity’s own script: if ( this . isClicked ) { this . sprite . opacity = 0.5 ; } } Touch The global touch surface is array-like. Each active touch has id , world/screen coordinates, start coordinates, dx , dy , distance , justStarted and justEnded . js function onUpdate () { for ( var t of touch ) { if ( t . justStarted ) { debug . log ( "Touch " + t . id , t . x + ", " + t . y ); } } if ( touch . tappedOn ( this . name )) { this . spawn ( "Explosion" , { x : this . x , y : this . y }); } } Gestures Gesture Properties touch.swipe active, direction, dx, dy, distance; active after >40 px movement. touch.pinch active, scale, delta, distance for two-finger gestures. js function onUpdate () { if ( touch . swipe . active && touch . swipe . direction === "left" ) { scene . load ( "NextLevel" ); } if ( touch . pinch . active ) { this . camera . zoom *= touch . pinch . scale ; // pinch-to-zoom } } Virtual joysticks The Joystick component exposes normalized read-only x , y , magnitude , angle and active values. This works well with Car controllers and custom movement scripts. js // Script attached to an entity with a Joystick component: function onUpdate () { if ( this . joystick . active ) { this . controller . simulateMove ( this . joystick . x , this . joystick . y ); } }

title: Lifecycle
description: Complete Realot Studio script lifecycle and callback reference.
content: Core lifecycle Callback Semantics onStart() Once before first onUpdate(). onClone() Once for runtime clones, immediately before onStart(). onUpdate(dt) Every render frame. onFixedUpdate(dt) Fixed 60 Hz accumulator. onDestroy() Before entity removal / scene end. js function onStart () { this . hp = 100 ; // custom fields on this persist across the entity’s lifetime debug . log ( "HP" , this . hp ); } function onUpdate () { this . x += 50 * time . deltaTime ; // frame-rate independent movement } function onFixedUpdate ( dt ) { // runs at a fixed 60 Hz step — good for deterministic physics-adjacent logic } function onDestroy () { debug . clear ( "HP" ); } Pointer callbacks onClick() is a frame pulse for mouse/finger presses targeting an entity with Collider2D. For continuous polling, use this.isPointerOver , this.isClicked , this.isTouchOver or this.isTapped where appropriate. js function onClick () { this . destroy (); // pops this entity when clicked or tapped } Collision callbacks Callback Runs onCollision(other) Alias of collision-enter behavior. onCollisionEnter(other) Contact begins. onCollisionStay(other) Every physics step while still touching. onCollisionExit(other) Contact ends. onTriggerEnter(other) Trigger overlap begins. onTriggerExit(other) Trigger overlap ends. js function onCollisionEnter ( other ) { if ( other . name === "Ground" ) this . isGrounded = true ; } function onTriggerEnter ( other ) { if ( other . hasComponent ( "Rigidbody2D" )) scene . load ( "Level2" ); } State callbacks When using this.state.change(name) , Realot Studio can call onStateExit() , onStateEnter() and onStateUpdate(dt) for state-specific logic. js function onUpdate () { if ( this . hp <= 0 && this . state . current !== "dead" ) { this . state . change ( "dead" ); } } function onStateEnter () { if ( this . state . current === "dead" ) this . sprite . opacity = 0.3 ; } Error isolation Lifecycle errors are caught and reported by the runtime. A one-time onStart() failure disables the script; recurring onUpdate() errors are isolated so the next frame can continue.
